source.title: The global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for unitary groups: the endoscopic case
source.authors: Raphaël Beuzart-Plessis, Pierre-Henri Chaudouard and Michał Zydor
readSections: The published version, read in full: the open-access (CC BY 4.0) PDF from Centre Mersenne, https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-021-00129-1.pdf (107 PDF pages, journal pp. 183–336; SHA-256 a07a6143d3e71f1eca31b6ba9b774bec325a7de07c7417b7796486a77df13794; fetched 23 September 2026). Read: §1 Introduction (Theorems 1.1.5.1, 1.1.5.3, 1.1.6.1 and the announcements 1.2.3.1–1.3.3.2), §2 Preliminaries (measures, heights and weights, function spaces, Fourier coefficients, automorphic forms, relative characters, cuspidal data, kernels), §3 the coarse spectral expansion of the Jacquet–Rallis trace formula for Schwartz functions, §4 Flicker–Rallis periods of spectral kernels, §5 the ∗-regular contribution, §6 the Flicker–Rallis zeta integrals, §7 the canonical extension of the Rankin–Selberg period, §8 the second proof, §9 the local and global Flicker–Rallis functional comparison, §10 the proofs of the Gan–Gross–Prasad and Ichino–Ikeda conjectures, Appendix A (topological vector spaces) and the references. Page numbers below are the journal's; pages checked against page images where a misprint is recorded.

arXiv 2007.05601 has a single version (v1, 10 July 2020, 101 pages); its TeX source (e-print SHA-256 5e0065cda3ddc1289a8d89c2ebf802ff2dfc1a02635515ffa15482df2b3e66bf) was fetched but the published version, which is freely available and substantially revised (it adds §3 on Schwartz test functions and §8's second proof), is the version extracted.

To check the citations of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, the PDFs of arXiv 1912.07169 v1 and v2 were compared with v3 (the Annals text, extracted as PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21), including the source of its Proposition 4.13 and Theorem 4.14.

Other cited inputs (Zydor, Chaudouard–Zydor, Ichino–Yamana, Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski, Lapid, Flicker, Feigon–Lapid–Offen, Beuzart-Plessis, R. N. Harris, Mok, KMSW, Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry, Grothendieck, Trèves) were not read; items resting on them state them as the paper uses them.

summary: The paper proves the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture (Theorem 1.1.5.1) and the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for tempered representations (Theorem 1.1.6.1) for U(n) × U(n+1) in all endoscopic cases, that is for every Hermitian Arthur parameter Π = Ind(Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_r) of GL_n(A_E) × GL_{n+1}(A_E), not only cuspidal ones. The method is the Jacquet–Rallis comparison with the isolation multipliers of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu. Its new content is the linear side. §3 extends Zydor's coarse spectral expansion to Schwartz test functions and gives three truncated expressions for each I_χ. For the ∗-regular cuspidal datum χ of Π, the contribution is discrete, I_χ = 2^{−dim a_P}I_Π. It is proved twice: by truncation, through Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski intertwining periods and Ichino–Yamana regularised Rankin–Selberg periods (§§4–5); and by zeta integrals, through the residue of Flicker's Asai integral and a canonical extension of the Rankin–Selberg period to moderate-growth functions (§§6–8). A local unfolding (§9) identifies the two relative characters. The atlas plans Arthur's notation, truncation and (G, M)-families (AA, AS.3, AS.6), the spectral decomposition (AS.4), Eisenstein series (AS.1–AS.2), automorphic forms (AF), Rankin–Selberg theory (AL.3), Mok/KMSW (ML.4) and the GRS descent (ML.5). The Jacquet–Rallis comparison, the isolation Part II and the Gan–Gross–Prasad framework are pending candidates, and this extraction extends them. Asai L-functions and the periods of Eisenstein series on general linear groups are planned nowhere; they become a new Part II of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors. Ten source issues are recorded. The one of substance (E1): the final argument invokes Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu Theorem 4.14(4) for a non-cuspidal base change, which is exactly where that theorem's printed proof has a gap.

items.name: Hermitian spaces and the unitary pairs U′_h ⊂ U_h
items.statement: E/F is a quadratic extension of number fields with Galois involution c and quadratic idèle class character η. ℋ_n is the set of isomorphism classes of non-degenerate c-hermitian spaces over E of rank n, and h_0 ∈ ℋ_1 is the norm form N_{E/F}. For h ∈ ℋ_n: U′_h = U(h), U_h = U(h) × U(h ⊕ h_0), with the diagonal embedding U′_h ↪ U_h. [H] = H(F)∖H(A) carries the quotient of a Haar measure by the counting measure.
items.note: The relevant pairs of GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups specialised to U(n) × U(n+1) with W⊥ of dimension 1; hermitian forms come from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2.

items.name: Hermitian Arthur parameters of G_n = Res_{E/F} GL_n and the group S_Π
items.statement: A Hermitian Arthur parameter of G_n (strictly, a generic discrete one) is an irreducible automorphic representation Π for which there are a partition n_1 + ⋯ + n_r = n and cuspidal Π_i of G_{n_i}(A) with: (1) each Π_i conjugate self-dual with L(s, Π_i, As^{(−1)^{n+1}}) having a pole at s = 1; (2) the Π_i mutually non-isomorphic; (3) Π ≅ Ind^{G_n}_P(Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_r) (full normalised induction, P with Levi G_{n_1} × ⋯ × G_{n_r}). r and the Π_i are unique up to order, and S_Π = (ℤ/2)^r. For G = G_n × G_{n+1}, a Hermitian Arthur parameter is Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} with Π_i one for G_i, and S_Π = S_{Π_n} × S_{Π_{n+1}}.
items.note: Extends the cuspidal 'hermitian' representations of Definition 1.5 of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu to isobaric sums; S_Π is the component group of the generic discrete parameter. Arthur parameters themselves are ML.4.

items.name: Weak (and strong) base change from U_h to G
items.statement: For h ∈ ℋ_n and σ a cuspidal automorphic representation of U_h(A), a Hermitian Arthur parameter Π of G is a weak base change of σ, written Π = BC(σ), if Π_v is the split local base change of σ_v for almost all places v of F split in E. By Mok and Kaletha–Mínguez–Shin–White a σ with a weak base change has a strong one (Π_v the local base change of σ_v at every v), and by Ramakrishnan a weak base change is automatically strong; the theorems are stated with the weak notion to keep them independent of Mok and KMSW.
items.note: Definition 1.6 of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, already added to this candidate, is the same notion; here the target is a Hermitian Arthur parameter rather than a hermitian cuspidal representation.

items.name: Local normalised periods P♮_{h,σ_v} and the Ichino–Ikeda L-value 𝓛(s, σ)
items.statement: For σ = ⊗′σ_v cuspidal on U_h(A), tempered everywhere, with (strong) base change Π: 𝓛(s, σ) = ∏_{i=1}^{n+1} L(s + i − ½, η^i) · L(s, Π)/L(s + ½, σ, Ad) (completed; Ad via the local Langlands correspondence of Mok, KMSW), and 𝓛(s, σ_v) its local quotient. For an invariant inner product (·,·)_v on σ_v and a Haar measure on U′_h(F_v): P♮_{h,σ_v}(φ_v, φ′_v) = 𝓛(½, σ_v)^{−1} ∫_{U′_h(F_v)} (σ_v(h_v)φ_v, φ′_v)_v dh_v, absolutely convergent by temperedness (R. N. Harris, Prop. 2.1), and 𝓛(s, σ_v) has neither zero nor pole at s = ½. For φ = ⊗′φ_v, P♮_{h,σ_v}(φ_v, φ_v) = vol(U′_h(O_v))(φ_v, φ_v)_v for almost all v (Harris, Thm. 2.12) (1.1.6.1). The Petersson product is (φ, φ)_Pet = ∫_{[U_h]} |φ|².
items.note: The ingredients of the refined (Ichino–Ikeda) conjecture in Harris's formulation, which Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu added to this candidate; the local absolute convergence and unramified computation are Harris's theorems, imported as cited.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.5.1: the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for U(n) × U(n+1) (all Hermitian Arthur parameters)
items.statement: Let Π be a Hermitian Arthur parameter of G = G_n × G_{n+1}. Then the following are equivalent: (1) the complete Rankin–Selberg L-function satisfies L(½, Π) ≠ 0 (all places, including archimedean ones); (2) there are h ∈ ℋ_n and an irreducible cuspidal automorphic subrepresentation σ of U_h such that Π is a weak base change of σ and the period 𝒫_h(φ) = ∫_{[U′_h]} φ(h) dh is a non-zero linear form on σ.
items.note: The simple (cuspidal Π) case is Theorem 1.8 of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu (cited here as its Theorem 1.7, see sourceIssues E2). The proof uses Proposition 10.1.6.1, which invokes BPLZZ Theorem 4.14(4) in the non-cuspidal case where its printed proof has a gap (sourceIssues E1). Proved statement of the consumer of GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.5.3: non-vanishing of central Rankin–Selberg values
items.statement: Let Π_{n+1} be a Hermitian Arthur parameter of G_{n+1}. There is a simple (cuspidal) Hermitian Arthur parameter Π_n of G_n with L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0.
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 1.1.5.1 word for word as W. Zhang (Ann. of Math. 180 (2014), Thm. 1.2), via the Burger–Sarnak trick and automorphic descent; the paper gives no further proof.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.6.1: the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for tempered σ on U(n) × U(n+1)
items.statement: Let σ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of U_h, tempered at every place, and Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} its weak (hence strong) base change to G. Normalise 𝒫_h and (·,·)_Pet by the Tamagawa measures (which include the global normalising L-values, §2.3) and let the local Haar measures dh_v on U′_h(F_v) factorise the Tamagawa measure. Then for every non-zero factorisable φ = ⊗′φ_v ∈ σ: |𝒫_h(φ)|²/(φ, φ)_Pet = |S_Π|^{−1} 𝓛(½, σ) ∏_v P♮_{h,σ_v}(φ_v, φ_v)/(φ_v, φ_v)_v.
items.note: The product is well defined by (1.1.6.1). Proved for cuspidal Π (|S_Π| = 4) by Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu. The proof reduces by W. Zhang's Lemma 1.7 (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27 (2014)) to the identity (10.3.2.1) of relative characters.

items.name: Arthur's notation for parabolic subgroups, chambers and truncation parameters
items.statement: For G reductive over F with minimal parabolic P_0 = M_0N_0: a*_G = X*(G) ⊗ ℝ, a_G = Hom(X*(G), ℝ), H_G: G(A) → a_G with ⟨χ, H_G(g)⟩ = log|χ(g)|, G(A)^1 = ker H_G; for semi-standard P the Harish-Chandra map H_P: G(A) → a_P through the Iwasawa decomposition G(A) = P(A)K; the decompositions a_P = a^Q_P ⊕ a_Q, a*_P = a^{Q,*}_P ⊕ a*_Q; ρ^Q_P, δ^Q_P; the simple roots Δ^Q_P, coroots Δ^{Q,∨}_P, weights Δ̂^Q_P and the characteristic functions τ^Q_P, τ̂^Q_P; Weyl sets W(P, Q) and 𝒫(M); a truncation parameter T ∈ a_0 with ⟨α, T⟩ large for α ∈ Δ_0 and its translates T_P; Siegel domains 𝔰_P = ω_0{a ∈ A^∞_0 : ⟨α, H_0(a)⟩ ≥ ⟨α, T_−⟩, α ∈ Δ^P_0}K with G(A) = M_P(F)N_P(A)𝔰_P.
items.note: Notation of Arthur (Duke 1978, §§5–6); the character spaces and H_G are AA.2, Siegel domains AA.3 and the chambers and truncation parameter AS.3.

items.name: Haar and Tamagawa measures, with the global normalising L-values
items.statement: a_P gets the Haar measure giving Hom(X*(P), ℤ) covolume 1 and ia*_P the dual measure, so vol(ia*_P/iX*(P)) = (2π)^{−dim a_P}; θ_P(λ) = vol(a^G_P/ℤ(Δ^∨_P))^{−1} ∏_{α∈Δ_P} ⟨λ, α^∨⟩. For a connected linear algebraic group H over F, choose a rational invariant volume form ω_H and ψ′; the local measures dh_v = |ω_H|_{ψ′_v} satisfy vol(H(O_v)) = Δ_{H,v}^{−1} for almost all v, where Δ_{H,v} = L_{H,v}(0) and L_H is Gross's Artin–Tate L-function of H; the Tamagawa measure is dh = (Δ*_H)^{−1} ∏_v Δ_{H,v} dh_v with Δ*_H = L*_H(0) the leading coefficient, and partial versions dh^S = (Δ^{S,*}_H)^{−1} ∏_{v∉S} Δ_{H,v} dh_v give dh = dh_S × dh^S. For GL_n, L_H(s) = ζ_F(s + 1)⋯ζ_F(s + n) and ω_H = (det h)^{−n} ∧ dh_{ij}. [G], [G]_P and [G]_{P,0} = A^∞_P∖[G]_P carry the induced quotient (semi-invariant) measures.
items.note: AA.2 constructs Tamagawa measures from invariant forms and convergence factors; the normalisation by L*_H(0) of Gross's motive must be recorded explicitly, since the paper's Tamagawa measures include the global L-values (footnote 3). The GL_n form is printed (det h)^{−1}∧dh_{ij} (sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Heights on G(A), on [G]_P and on adelic vector spaces
items.statement: From a faithful ι: G ↪ GL_N, ‖g‖ = ∏_v max_{i,j}(|ι(g)_{ij}|_v, |ι(g^{−1})_{ij}|_v), independent up to powers of the choice; 1 ≪ ‖g‖, ‖gh‖ ≪ ‖g‖‖h‖, ‖g‖ = ‖g^{−1}‖. ‖x‖_P = inf_{γ ∈ M_P(F)N_P(A)} ‖γx‖ and σ_P = 1 + log‖·‖_P on [G]_P, with ‖x‖_Q ≪ ‖x‖_P for P ⊂ Q, ‖g‖_P ∼ ‖g‖ on Siegel domains, ‖m‖_{M_P} ∼ ‖m‖_P, compatibility with reductive subgroups (2.4.1.5) and ‖a‖ ≪ ‖ax‖_P for a ∈ A^∞_P, H_P(x) = 0 (2.4.1.6). For a finite-dimensional F-vector space V with basis v_i, ‖Σx_iv_i‖_V = ∏_v max(1, |x_1|_v, …, |x_d|_v).
items.note: Height functions from faithful embeddings and their comparability are AF.0; the estimates on Siegel domains are AA.3 (Mœglin–Waldspurger I.2.2).

items.name: Weights on [G]_P and Franke's weights d_{P,λ}
items.statement: A weight on [G]_P is a positive measurable w with w(xk) ∼ w(x) for k in any compact subset of G(A) (Bernstein, Franke). Lemma 2.4.3.1: every weight satisfies w(xg) ≪ w(x)‖g‖^{N_0} for some N_0. By Franke (Prop. 2.1), for λ ∈ a*_0 there is a weight d_{P,λ} ∼ exp⟨λ, H_0(x)⟩ on Siegel domains, with d_{P,tλ} ∼ d_{P,λ}^t, d_{P,λ+μ} ∼ d_{P,λ}d_{P,μ}, d_{P,λ} ≪ d_{P,μ} if λ ≺_P μ, and ‖x‖_P ∼ max_{λ∈Λ^P_ι} d_{P,λ}(x) (2.4.3.13). Lemma 2.4.3.2: for λ ∈ a*^{P+}_0, d_{P,λ}(x) ∼ sup_{γ∈P(F)} e^{⟨λ, H_0(γx)⟩}; Corollary 2.4.3.3: d_{Q,λ} ≪ d_{P,λ} on Q(F)∖G(A) for Q ⊂ P.
items.note: Weighted L²-analysis on [G]_P (Franke, Ann. Sci. ENS 1998) is not planned; it is the frame for the function spaces of this Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.4.1: reduction theory near infinity
items.statement: For standard P ⊂ Q and the natural projections π^Q_P: P(F)N_Q(A)∖G(A) → [G]_P and π^P_Q → [G]_Q, with ω^Q_P[> C] = {d^Q_P > C} where d^Q_P(x) = min_{α∈Σ^Q_P} d_{P,α}(x): (1) for some ε > 0, π^P_Q maps ω^Q_P[> ε] onto [G]_Q; (2) on ω^Q_P[> ε], d_{P,λ} ∼ d_{Q,λ}, d^Q_P ∼ d^P_Q and ‖·‖_P ∼ ‖·‖_Q; (3) the fibres of π^P_Q on ω^Q_P[> ε] have at most cε^{−r} points; (4) for every ε there is C with π^P_Q injective on pairs in ω^Q_P[> ε] × ω^Q_P[> C]; (5) π^P_Q is a local measure-preserving homeomorphism and π^Q_P is proper, pushing the invariant measure forward to the invariant measure.
items.note: Siegel domains and Langlands's Lemmas 2.11–2.12 (Springer LNM 544): the reduction theory of AA.3, 'finite intersection properties' included.

items.name: Neighbourhoods of infinity: the weights d^Q_P, d^P_Q and their restriction to subgroups
items.statement: For standard P ⊂ Q with Σ^Q_P the roots of A_0 in 𝔫_P/𝔫_Q: d^Q_P(x) = min_{α∈Σ^Q_P} d_{P,α}(x) on [G]_P and d^P_Q(x) = min_{α∈Σ^Q_P} d_{Q,α}(x) on [G]_Q, with d^Q_P(x) ≪ min_{α∈Δ^Q_0∖Δ^P_0} d_{P,α}(x) ≪ max(d^Q_P, (d^Q_P)^{1/n}) and d^Q_P ≪ d^P_Q on P(F)N_Q(A)∖G(A) (2.4.4.19). Lemma 2.4.4.2: for H ⊂ G reductive with P_H = P ∩ H, Q_H = Q ∩ H parabolic with unipotent radicals N_P ∩ H, N_Q ∩ H, d^Q_P(h) ≪ d^{Q_H}_{P_H}(h) on [H]_{P_H}, with equivalence when G = Res_{K/F}H_K and P, Q are the restrictions of scalars.
items.note: Used throughout §3 for the Jacquet–Rallis weights; general reduction-theory statements stay in AA.3.

items.name: Harish-Chandra's Ξ-function on [G]_P
items.statement: Ξ^P(x) = vol_{[G]_P}(xU)^{−1/2} for a compact neighbourhood U of 1 (independent up to equivalence), Ξ^P ∼ d_{P,ρ_0} (2.4.5.23), ∫_{[G]_P} Ξ^P(g)² σ_P(g)^{−d_0} dg < ∞ for some d_0 (Lapid 2013, §2 (9)) (2.4.5.24), and Ξ^P(g) ≪ ‖g‖^{N_0}_P (2.4.5.25).
items.note: The global Ξ-function of Lapid's Harish-Chandra Schwartz space of G(F)∖G(A).

items.name: The global Schwartz space 𝒮(G(A)) as a convolution algebra
items.statement: For compact C ⊂ G(A_f) and compact-open J ⊂ K^∞, 𝒮(G(A), C, J) is the Fréchet space of smooth J-bi-invariant f supported in G(F_∞) × C with ‖f‖_{r,X,Y} = sup_g ‖g‖^r |(R(X)L(Y)f)(g)| < ∞ for all r and X, Y ∈ 𝒰(𝔤_∞); 𝒮(G(A)) is their locally convex direct limit, a strict LF space and an algebra under convolution containing C_c^∞(G(A)) densely; C^r_c(G(A)) is spanned by products f_∞f^∞ with f_∞ of class C^r compactly supported. 𝒮(A^n) is defined with the height ‖·‖_{A^n}.
items.note: Coalesces with the Schwartz test functions of Definition 3.1 of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu in this Part II.

items.name: F-, SF- and SLF-representations of G(A) and smooth vectors
items.statement: A Fréchet representation V of G(A) is an F-representation if its topology is given by seminorms for each of which the action is continuous (Bernstein–Krötz); v is smooth if g ↦ gv is smooth, V^∞ is invariant and (V^∞)^J with the seminorms v ↦ ‖Xv‖ is an SF representation of G(F_∞), making V^∞ a strict LF space. An SLF representation is a G(A)-space V with Fréchet structures on each V^J making V^J an SF representation of G(F_∞), V = ∪_J V^J and V^J ⊂ V^{J′} closed. 𝒮(G(A)) acts by f·v = ∫ f(g) g·v dg and V^∞ = 𝒮(G(A))·V (Dixmier–Malliavin) (2.5.3.2). Lemma 2.5.4.1: a closed invariant subspace of an SLF representation is SLF and its LF topology is the induced one; hence equivariant morphisms of SLF representations with closed image are embeddings.
items.note: The representation-theoretic frame for all function spaces of §§2.5–2.9.

items.name: The Dixmier–Malliavin theorem
items.statement: Every smooth vector of a (smooth Fréchet) representation of a real Lie group is a finite sum of vectors π(f)v with f ∈ C_c^∞; hence V^∞ = 𝒮(G(A))·V for every F- or SLF-representation of G(A), and 𝒮(G(A)) = 𝒮(G(A)) ∗ C_c^∞(G(A)).
items.locator: (2.5.3.2), p. 210; used in Lemma 2.5.11.1, Corollary 2.5.15.2, Theorem 2.9.8.1 and Proposition 3.4.3.1
items.note: Dixmier–Malliavin, Bull. Sci. Math. 102 (1978). PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 routes the same lemma as a source of AF.1; this route coalesces with it.

items.name: Weighted L²-spaces and the Sobolev inequality on [G]_P
items.statement: For a weight w on [G]_P, L²_w([G]_P) is the Hilbert space of functions square-integrable for w(g)dg, a continuous representation of G(A); its smooth vectors satisfy |φ(g)| ≪ Ξ^P(g)w(g)^{−1/2} (Bernstein's key lemma) (2.5.5.4); every continuous linear form T on L²_w([G]_P)^∞ and f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)) give φ ∈ L²_{w^{−1}}([G]_P)^∞ with T(R(f)ψ) = ⟨ψ, φ⟩_P (2.5.5.5); notation L²_{N,w} = L²_{‖·‖^N_P w}, L²_{σ,d,w} = L²_{σ^d_P w}. Proposition 2.5.5.1: there is d_0 ≥ 0 such that L²_{σ,d_0,w}([G]_P)^{∞,J} ⊂ L²_w([G]_P)^{∞,J} is nuclear for every J and w (Bernstein 1988), so summable families there become absolutely summable.
items.note: Bernstein, On the support of Plancherel measure (1988), p. 688 and §3.4.

items.name: Function spaces on [G]_P: 𝒮, 𝒞, 𝒯 and their weighted variants
items.statement: 𝒮_0([G]_P) (rapid decay, seminorms sup ‖x‖^N_P|φ|), 𝒮_{00} its continuous functions; the Schwartz space 𝒮([G]_P) (smooth, sup ‖x‖^N_P|R(X)φ| < ∞) = 𝒮_{00}([G]_P)^∞ = ∩_N L²_N([G]_P)^∞; the Harish-Chandra Schwartz space 𝒞([G]_P) (sup Ξ^P(x)^{−1}σ_P(x)^d|R(X)φ| < ∞) = ∩_d L²_{σ,d}([G]_P)^∞; 𝒯^0_w([G]_P) (Radon measures with ∫w^{−1}|φ| < ∞) and 𝒯^0 = ∪_N 𝒯^0_N, dual to 𝒮_{00}; 𝒯_w([G]_P) (sup w^{−1}|R(X)φ| < ∞), the uniform moderate growth space 𝒯([G]_P) = ∪_N 𝒯_N([G]_P) = ∪_N L²_{−N}([G]_P)^∞; 𝒮_{w,N}([G]_P) (sup ‖x‖^{−N}_P w(x)^r|R(X)φ| < ∞ for all r) and 𝒮_w = ∪_N 𝒮_{w,N} = ∪_N ∩_r L²_{−N,w^r}([G]_P)^∞, all SLF representations. 𝒮 is dense in 𝒞, 𝒯 and 𝒮_w (but usually not in 𝒯_N or 𝒮_{w,N}). Lemma 2.5.11.1: if φ ∈ 𝒯^0([G]_P) and w is bounded on its support then R(f)φ ∈ 𝒮_w([G]_P) for f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)).
items.note: The Harish-Chandra Schwartz space of G(F)∖G(A) is Lapid's (TIFR 2013), there written 𝒮(G(F)∖G(A)); uniform moderate growth for all derivatives is also named in AF.0, which does not plan these topologies.

items.name: Nuclearity and tensor-product decompositions of 𝒮([G]) and 𝒞([G])
items.statement: For every compact-open J, 𝒮([G]_P)^J and 𝒞([G]_P)^J are nuclear Fréchet spaces (Bernstein 1988, end of §3.5; Casselman 1989). For G = G_1 × G_2 and J = J_1 × J_2 there are topological isomorphisms 𝒮([G_1])^{J_1} ⊗̂ 𝒮([G_2])^{J_2} ≃ 𝒮([G])^J and 𝒞([G_1])^{J_1} ⊗̂ 𝒞([G_2])^{J_2} ≃ 𝒞([G])^J sending φ_1 ⊗ φ_2 to (g_1, g_2) ↦ φ_1(g_1)φ_2(g_2); so continuous forms L_1, L_2 on 𝒞([G_i]) give L_1 ⊗̂ L_2 on 𝒞([G]).
items.note: Proved by Grothendieck's description of completed tensor products (A.0.7.8) as in Beuzart-Plessis's Astérisque 418, Prop. 4.4.1(v).

items.name: Constant terms and pseudo-Eisenstein series on 𝒮_0 and 𝒯^0
items.statement: For standard P ⊂ Q: the G(A)-equivariant continuous maps E^Q_P: 𝒮_0([G]_P) → 𝒮_0([G]_Q), E^Q_P(φ)(x) = Σ_{γ∈P(F)∖Q(F)} φ(γx), and φ ↦ φ_P: 𝒯^0([G]_Q) → 𝒯^0([G]_P), on 𝒯([G]_Q) given by φ_P(x) = ∫_{[N_P]} φ(ux) du; E^Q_P sends 𝒮([G]_P) into 𝒮([G]_Q), φ ↦ φ_P sends 𝒯_N([G]_Q) into 𝒯_N([G]_P), and ⟨φ_P, ψ⟩_P = ⟨φ, E^Q_P(ψ)⟩_Q (2.5.13.12). Lemma 2.5.13.1: there is c > 0 with φ ↦ sup_x δ^Q_P(x)^{cN}‖x‖^N_P|φ_P(x)| a continuous seminorm on 𝒮_0([G]_Q) for every N.
items.note: Constant terms of automorphic forms are AF.3; their extension to these measure and function spaces and the adjoint pseudo-Eisenstein map are new here.

items.name: Proposition 2.5.14.1: approximation by the constant term
items.statement: (1) For N > 0, r ≥ 0 and X ∈ 𝒰(𝔤_∞) there is a continuous seminorm ‖·‖_{N,X,r} on 𝒯_N([G]_Q) with |R(X)φ(x) − R(X)φ_P(x)| ≤ ‖x‖^N_P d^Q_P(x)^{−r}‖φ‖_{N,X,r} for x ∈ P(F)N_Q(A)∖G(A). (2) For a weight w on [G]_Q and φ ∈ L²_w([G]_Q)^∞ there is N with ∫_{A^∞_Q} |φ(ax) − φ_P(ax)|² w(a)δ_Q(a)^{−1} da ≪_r ‖x‖^N_P d^Q_P(x)^{−r} for every r.
items.note: Reformulates Mœglin–Waldspurger, Ann. Sci. ENS 1989, Lemma I.2.10, iterated along a flag of maximal parabolics.

items.name: Proposition 2.5.15.1 and Corollary 2.5.15.2: weighted constant terms and pseudo-Eisenstein series
items.statement: For P ⊂ Q and every weight w on [G]_Q there are weights w^±_P on [G]_P with φ ↦ φ_P continuous L²_w([G]_Q) → L²_{w^−_P}([G]_P), E^Q_P extending continuously L²_{w^+_P}([G]_P) → L²_w([G]_Q), and w^+_P ∼ w ∼ w^−_P on ω^Q_P[> ε] for every ε > 0. If w, w′ agree on A^∞_Q: for w′ ≪ w, φ ↦ ((φ_P)_{P⊊Q}, φ) is a closed embedding L²_w([G]_Q)^∞ → ∏_{P⊊Q} L²_{w^−_P}([G]_P)^∞ × L²_{w′}([G]_Q)^∞; dually, for w′ ≫ w, ((φ_P), φ) ↦ φ + Σ_{P⊊Q} E^Q_P(φ_P) is an open surjection onto L²_w([G]_Q)^∞.
items.note: Partly after Franke 1998, §4, p. 204; the induction step of Theorem 2.9.4.1.

items.name: Lemma 2.6.1.1: decay of Fourier coefficients along unipotent radicals
items.statement: Let V_P be the additive characters N_P → G_a, ℓ ∈ V_P(F), ψ_ℓ = ψ ∘ ℓ_A and φ_{N_P,ψ_ℓ}(g) = ∫_{[N_P]} φ(ug)ψ_ℓ(u)^{−1} du. (1) There is c > 0 such that for all N_1, N_2 ≥ 0, φ ↦ sup_{m∈M_P(A)} ‖Ad*(m^{−1})ℓ‖^{N_1}_{V_P}‖m‖^{N_2}_{M_P}δ_P(m)^{cN_2}|φ_{N_P,ψ_ℓ}(m)| is a continuous seminorm on 𝒮([G]); (2) for N > 0 and every N_1, φ ↦ sup_m ‖Ad*(m^{−1})ℓ‖^{N_1}_{V_P}‖m‖^{−N}_{M_P}|φ_{N_P,ψ_ℓ}(m)| is a continuous seminorm on 𝒯_N([G]).
items.note: The convergence input for the Flicker–Rallis and Rankin–Selberg zeta integrals of §§6–7; the local facts (2.6.1.3)–(2.6.1.4) are left to the reader.

items.name: Lemma 2.6.2.1: convergence of the mirabolic Epstein-type integral
items.statement: With P_n the mirabolic subgroup of GL_n (stabiliser of e_n = (0, …, 0, 1) for the right action) and A^∞_{GL_n} ≅ ℝ_{>0}: for C > 1 and N_1, N_2 ≫_C 1, ∫_{P_n(F)∖GL_n(A)×ℝ_{>0}} ‖ag‖^{−N_1}_{GL_n}‖e_n g‖^{−N_2}_{A^n}|det g|^s da dg converges for s ∈ ℋ_{]1,C[}, uniformly on closed vertical strips.
items.note: Uses ∫_{[GL_n]} ‖g‖^{−N} < ∞ (Beuzart-Plessis, JIMJ 2021, Prop. A.1.1(vi)).

items.name: Spaces of automorphic forms 𝒜_P(G) with their SLF topologies
items.statement: 𝒜_P(G) is the space of 𝒵(𝔤_∞)-finite functions in 𝒯([G]_P); 𝒜_{P,cusp}(G) (φ_Q = 0 for all Q ⊊ P) and 𝒜_{P,disc}(G) (|φ| ∈ L²([G]_{P,0})); for an ideal 𝒥 ⊂ 𝒵(𝔤_∞) of finite codimension 𝒜_{P,𝒥}(G) is closed in some 𝒯_N([G]_P), with the induced topology (independent of N), and these are SLF representations; 𝒜_P(G) = ⊕_𝔪 𝒜_P(G)_𝔪 over maximal ideals 𝔪, each a strict LF space.
items.note: Automorphic forms, cusp forms and square-integrable forms are AF.2–AF.3; the SLF topologies are part of the function-space layer of the AS Part II.

items.name: Cuspidal and discrete automorphic representations, their inductions and Petersson products
items.statement: A cuspidal (discrete) automorphic representation π of M_P(A) is a topologically irreducible subrepresentation of 𝒜_cusp(M_P) (𝒜_disc(M_P)), an SLF representation whose (𝔤_∞, K_∞)-module π^J_{(K_∞)} has π^J as its Casselman–Wallach globalisation; twists π_λ (λ ∈ a*_{P,ℂ}); isotypic parts 𝒜_{π,cusp}(M_P), 𝒜_{π,disc}(M_P); the normalised inductions Π = Ind^{G(A)}_{P(A)}(π) and 𝒜_{P,π,cusp}(G), 𝒜_{P,π,disc}(G), identified with forms φ ∈ 𝒜_P(G) with m ↦ e^{−⟨ρ_P,H_P(m)⟩}φ(mg) in π, the action I_P(λ) of 𝒮(G(A)) transported from π_λ, and the Petersson norm ‖φ‖²_Pet = ∫_{[G]_{P,0}} |φ|². For G = G_1 × G_2, Π^J = Π_1^{J_1} ⊗̂ Π_2^{J_2} (2.7.5.1).
items.note: Casselman–Wallach globalisation is AF.1 (Casselman; Wallach, Ch. 11; Bernstein–Krötz); automorphic representations and induced families AF.2 and AS.1.

items.name: Eisenstein series and intertwining operators for smooth discrete automorphic forms
items.statement: For φ ∈ 𝒜_{P,disc}(G) and λ ∈ a*_{P,ℂ}, E(g, φ, λ) = Σ_{δ∈P(F)∖G(F)} e^{⟨λ,H_P(δg)⟩}φ(δg) converges for Re λ in a cone and continues meromorphically to a*_{P,ℂ} (Langlands; Bernstein–Lapid for K_∞-finite φ; Lapid 2008 for smooth φ); at regular λ, φ ↦ E(φ, λ) is continuous Π → 𝒯_N([G]) for some N (Lapid 2008, Thm. 2.2, and the closed graph theorem). The intertwining operators M(w, λ): 𝒜_{P,disc}(G) → 𝒜_{Q,disc}(G), w ∈ W(P, Q), given by the usual integral over (N_Q ∩ wN_Pw^{−1})(A)∖N_Q(A), continue likewise.
items.note: AS.1–AS.2 plan convergence, meromorphic continuation and functional equations; the extension to smooth (not K_∞-finite) forms and the continuity into 𝒯_N([G]) of Lapid's 'A remark on Eisenstein series' must be included there.

items.name: Global Whittaker models of induced representations
items.statement: For G quasi-split and a non-degenerate character ψ_N of N_0(A) trivial on N_0(F), a ψ_N-generic Π (with a continuous ψ_N-equivariant form ℓ) is isomorphic to W(Π, ψ_N) = {g ↦ ℓ(Π(g)φ)}, topologised from Π; for G = G_1 × G_2, W(Π_1, ψ_1)^{J_1} ⊗̂ W(Π_2, ψ_2)^{J_2} ≃ W(Π, ψ_N)^J.
items.note: AL.3 plans global and archimedean Whittaker functionals with completed tensor products.

items.name: Proposition 2.8.4.1: relative characters of Schwartz functions converge
items.statement: Let B: 𝒜_{P,π}(G) × 𝒜_{P,π}(G) → ℂ be continuous sesquilinear (𝒜_{P,π} cuspidal or discrete) and ω ⊂ a^{G,*}_P compact. For f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)) and any K-basis ℬ_{P,π} (union over τ ∈ K̂ of Petersson-orthonormal bases of the τ-isotypic parts), Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} I_P(λ, f)φ ⊗ φ̄ converges absolutely in 𝒜_{P,π}(G) ⊗̂ 𝒜_{P,π}(G) uniformly for Re λ ∈ ω, so J_B(λ, f) = Σ_φ B(I_P(λ, f)φ, φ) converges absolutely, independently of the basis; and f ↦ J_B(λ, f) is continuous, with a single continuous seminorm on 𝒮(G(A), C, K_0) bounding it for Re λ ∈ ω (also for f ∈ C^r_c with r large, Remark 2.8.4.2).
items.note: Uses Wallach's Sobolev estimate (Real Reductive Groups II, §10.1) and the polynomial growth of dim 𝒜_{P,π}(G, K_0, τ) (Müller, GAFA 2000, Lemma 6.1).

items.name: Proposition 2.8.4.3: Arthur's factorisation of Schwartz functions
items.statement: For a normal open compact K_0 ⊂ K^∞ and m ≥ 1 there are Z ∈ 𝒰(𝔤_∞), g_1 ∈ C_c^∞(G(A)) and g_2 ∈ C^m_c(G(A)), invariant under K_∞-conjugation and K_0-bi-invariant, with f = f ∗ g_1 + (f ∗ Z) ∗ g_2 for every K_0-bi-invariant f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)); for m large, J_B(λ, f) = Σ_φ B(I_P(λ, f)φ, I_P(λ̄, g_1^∨)φ) + Σ_φ B(I_P(λ, f ∗ Z)φ, I_P(λ̄, g_2^∨)φ), both sums absolutely convergent.
items.note: Arthur, Duke 1978, Lemma 4.1 and Corollary 4.2, with a finite-dimensional computation.

items.name: Cuspidal data 𝔛(G)
items.statement: 𝔛(G) is the set of classes of pairs (M_P, π), P standard and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of M_P(A) with central character trivial on A^∞_P, under (M_P, π) ∼ (M_Q, τ) iff wπw^{−1} ≃ τ for some w ∈ W(P, Q); 𝔛(M_P) → 𝔛(G) is finite-to-one; χ^∨ is the class of (M_P, π^∨) (complex conjugate).
items.note: Cuspidal data index the decomposition of AS.4.

items.name: Langlands's decomposition of L²([G]_P) along cuspidal data
items.statement: For (M_P, π) ∈ X(G), 𝒮_π([G]_P) consists of φ ∈ 𝒮([G]_P) with φ_λ(x) = ∫_{A^∞_P} e^{−⟨ρ_P+λ, H_P(a)⟩}φ(ax) da ∈ 𝒜_{P,π_λ,cusp}(G) for all λ; L²_χ([G]_P) is the closure of the sum of E^P_{Q_i}(𝒮_{π_i}([G]_{Q_i})) over the (finite) preimage of χ in 𝔛(M_P), and L²_w([G]_P) = ⊕̂_{χ∈𝔛(G)} L²_{w,χ}([G]_P), L²([G]_{P,0}) = ⊕̂_χ L²_χ([G]_{P,0}) orthogonally (Mœglin–Waldspurger, Prop. II.2.4), for weights w on A^∞_P; the projections for two such weights agree on the intersection (2.9.2.2).
items.note: The decomposition over cuspidal data is AS.4; the version for weights on A^∞_P is a formal consequence.

items.name: Theorem 2.9.4.1: decomposition along cuspidal support in 𝒮, 𝒞, 𝒯 and 𝒮_w
items.statement: Let w be a weight on [G]_P and, for X ⊂ 𝔛(G), 𝒮_X([G]_P) = 𝒮([G]_P) ∩ L²_X([G]_P) and F_X([G]_P) the orthogonal of 𝒮_{X^c}([G]_P) in F([G]_P) for F ∈ {L²_w, 𝒞, 𝒯_N, 𝒯, 𝒮_{w,N}, 𝒮_w} (Lemma 2.9.3.1: E^P_Q(𝒮_X([G]_Q)) ⊂ 𝒮_X([G]_P) and 𝒯_X([G]_P)_Q ⊂ 𝒯_X([G]_Q)). (1) The orthogonal projection 𝒮([G]_P) → L²_X([G]_P) extends to a continuous projection L²_w([G]_P)^∞ → L²_{w,X}([G]_P)^∞, and (φ_χ)_{χ∈𝔛(G)} is summable with sum φ. (2) It restricts to a continuous projection 𝒮([G]_P) → 𝒮_X([G]_P) with (φ_χ) absolutely summable in 𝒮([G]_P). (3) For F ∈ {𝒞, 𝒯, 𝒮_w} it extends to F([G]_P) → F_X([G]_P) with ⟨φ_X, ψ⟩ = ⟨φ, ψ_X⟩ for (φ, ψ) ∈ 𝒯 × 𝒮, and there is N_0 with (φ_χ) absolutely summable in 𝒞([G]_P), 𝒯_{w,N_0}([G]_P) and 𝒮_{w,N+N_0}([G]_P) for φ in 𝒞, 𝒯_w and 𝒮_{w,N} respectively. Consequently 𝒮_X is dense in 𝒞_X and L²_{−N,X}([G]_P)^∞ (2.9.5.9), and for G = G_1 × G_2, 𝒮_{X_1}([G_1])^{J_1} ⊗̂ 𝒮_{X_2}([G_2])^{J_2} ≃ 𝒮_{X_1×X_2}([G])^J, likewise for 𝒞 (2.9.6.10).
items.note: A variation on Mœglin–Waldspurger III.2.6 and Franke–Schwermer for automorphic forms; proved by induction on the parabolic with Corollary 2.5.15.2 and the nuclearity of Proposition 2.5.5.1.

items.name: Regular cuspidal data: Proposition 2.9.7.1 and Corollary 2.9.7.2
items.statement: χ is regular if represented by (M_P, π) with wπ ≃ π for w ∈ W(P) only when w = 1; for GL_n and π = π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ π_k this means π_i ≠ π_j for i ≠ j. Proposition 2.9.7.1: for χ regular and P ⊂ G parabolic, φ ∈ L²_χ([G]) implies φ_P ∈ L²_χ([G]_P). Corollary 2.9.7.2: for χ regular, χ_M its preimage in 𝔛(M_P), φ ∈ 𝒮_χ([G]) and s ∈ ℋ_{>0}, φ_{P,s}(m) = δ_P(m)^{s−½}φ_P(m) lies in 𝒞_{χ_M}([M_P]), and s ↦ φ_{P,s} is holomorphic ℋ_{>0} → 𝒞_{χ_M}([M_P]).
items.note: The proof uses Mœglin–Waldspurger's inner product of pseudo-Eisenstein series (Prop. II.2.1), extended to smooth forms (footnote 5).

items.name: Theorem 2.9.8.1 (Lapid): spectral expansion of Harish-Chandra Schwartz functions for a regular datum
items.statement: Let G = ∏ Res_{K_i/F} GL_{n_i}, χ ∈ 𝔛(G) regular represented by (M_P, π), Π = Ind^{G(A)}_{P(A)}(π) = 𝒜_{P,π,cusp}(G) and ℬ_{P,π} a K-basis. There is N > 0 such that for φ ∈ 𝒞([G]) the series φ_{Π_λ} = Σ_{ψ∈ℬ_{P,π}} ⟨φ, E(ψ, λ)⟩_G E(ψ, λ) converges in 𝒯_N([G]) for every λ ∈ ia*_P, the function λ ↦ φ_{Π_λ} ∈ 𝒯_N([G]) is Schwartz (hence integrable), and φ = ∫_{ia*_P} φ_{Π_λ} dλ for φ ∈ 𝒞_χ([G]).
items.note: A restatement of part of Lapid, On the Harish-Chandra Schwartz space of G(F)∖G(A) (TIFR 2013), Prop. 5.1, Cor. 5.7 and Thm. 4.5, for groups satisfying Lapid's condition (HP) (general linear groups and their products).

items.name: Lemma 2.10.1.1: uniform bounds for the χ-parts of automorphic kernels
items.statement: K_{f,P}(x, y), K_{f,P,χ}, K^0_{f,P}, K^0_{f,P,χ} are the kernels of R(f) on L²([G]_P), L²_χ([G]_P), L²([G]_{P,0}), L²_χ([G]_{P,0}), with K^0_{f,P,χ}(x, y) = ∫_{A^∞_P} K_{f,P,χ}(x, ay)δ_P(a)^{−½} da. There is N_0 > 0 such that for every weight w on [G]_P and continuous seminorm ‖·‖_{w,N_0} on 𝒯_{w,N_0}([G]_P) there is a continuous seminorm ‖·‖_𝒮 on 𝒮(G(A)) with Σ_χ |K_{f,P,χ}(x, y)| ≤ ‖f‖_𝒮‖x‖^{N_0}_P w(x)w(y)^{−1}, the same for K^0 on [G]^1_P, and Σ_χ ‖K_{f,P,χ}(·, y)‖_{w,N_0} ≤ ‖f‖_𝒮 w(y)^{−1}.
items.note: Obtained from Theorem 2.9.4.1(3) by the uniform boundedness principle applied to Dirac measures.

items.name: Lemma 2.10.2.1: the spectral expansion of K^0_{f,χ} for Schwartz f
items.statement: There are a continuous seminorm ‖·‖ on 𝒮(G(A)) and N such that for X, Y ∈ 𝒰(𝔤_∞), x, y ∈ G(A)^1 and f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)): Σ_χ Σ_{P_0⊂P} |𝒫(M_P)|^{−1} ∫_{ia^{G,*}_P} Σ_{τ∈K̂} |Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,χ,τ}} R_x(X)E(x, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ) \overline{R_y(Y)E(y, φ, λ)}| dλ ≤ ‖L(X)R(Y)f‖ ‖x‖^N_G‖y‖^N_G, and K^0_{f,χ}(x, y) = Σ_{P_0⊂P} |𝒫(M_P)|^{−1} ∫_{ia^{G,*}_P} Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,χ}} E(x, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ)\overline{E(y, φ, λ)} dλ, with ℬ_{P,χ} a K-basis of the space 𝒜^0_{P,χ,disc}(G) of left A^∞_M-invariant discrete forms in L²_χ([G]_{P,0}).
items.note: Extends Arthur, Duke 1978, §4 (p. 931, Corollary 4.6, Lemma 4.8) to Schwartz functions.

items.name: The global Jacquet–Rallis setup on the linear side
items.statement: G′_n = GL_{n,F} ⊂ G_n = Res_{E/F}(GL_{n,E}); P′ ↦ P = Res_{E/F}(P′_E) is a bijection of standard parabolics with inverse P ↦ P ∩ G′_n; X*(P) has index 2^{dim a_P} in X*(P′), a_{P′} ≅ a_P with ⟨ρ^Q_P, H_P(x)⟩ = 2⟨ρ^{Q′}_{P′}, H_{P′}(x)⟩ on G′(A), and the Haar measure on A^∞_P is 2^{dim a_P} times that on A^∞_{P′} (Remark 3.1.3.1). G_n ⊂ G_{n+1} fixes e_{n+1}; G = G_n × G_{n+1}, G′ = G′_n × G′_{n+1}, H = ι(G_n) the diagonal, K = K_n × K_{n+1}; η_{G′}(g′) = η(det g′_n)^{n+1}η(det g′_{n+1})^n.
items.note: The global groups of the Jacquet–Rallis relative trace formula for GL_n × GL_{n+1} with the (H, (G′, η_{G′})) double period.

items.name: The Rankin–Selberg set F_RS, the signs ε^Q_P and the weights Δ_P, d^{Q,Δ}_P
items.statement: F_RS is the set of parabolics P = P_n × P_{n+1} of G with P_n standard in G_n, P_{n+1} semi-standard in G_{n+1} and P_{n+1} ∩ G_n = P_n; P_H = P ∩ H, P′ = P ∩ G′; for P ⊂ Q in F_RS, ε^Q_P = (−1)^{dim a^{Q_{n+1}}_{P_{n+1}}}. Weights on [G]_P: Δ_P(g) = inf_{γ∈M_{P_{n+1}}(F)N_{P_{n+1}}(A)} ‖g_n^{−1}γg_{n+1}‖ and d^{Q,Δ}_P(g) = min(d^{Q_{n+1}}_{P_{n+1}}(g_n), d^{Q_{n+1}}_{P_{n+1}}(g_{n+1})), with Δ_P ∼ 1 on [H]_{P_H}, d^{Q,Δ}_P ≪ d^Q_P, and w(g_{n+1}) ≪ w(g_n)Δ_P(g)^{N_0} for weights w on [G_{n+1}]_{P_{n+1}}. 'T sufficiently positive' means d(T) = inf_{α∈Δ_{n+1}} α(T) ≥ max(ε‖T‖, C).
items.note: Zydor's Rankin–Selberg set of parabolics (Crelle 2020).

items.name: Zydor's modified kernel K^T_{f,χ}
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)), χ ∈ 𝔛(G), T ∈ a_{n+1}: K^T_{f,χ}(h, g′) = Σ_{P∈F_RS} ε^G_P Σ_{γ∈P_H(F)∖H(F)} Σ_{δ∈P′(F)∖G′(F)} τ̂_{P_{n+1}}(H_{P_{n+1}}(δ_n g′_n) − T_{P_{n+1}}) K_{f,P,χ}(γh, δg′), with δ_ng′_n viewed in G′_{n+1}(A). For Schwartz f the sums are not finite but converge absolutely, using Σ_χ |K_{f,P,χ}(h, g′)| ≪_N ‖g′_n‖^{N′}_{P′_n}‖h‖^{−N}_{P_H}‖g′_{n+1}‖^{−N}_{P′_{n+1}} (3.2.3.2).
items.note: Zydor's kernel (Crelle 2020) for compactly supported functions; δ_n ranges over a finite set depending on g′_n (Arthur 1978, Lemma 5.1).

items.name: Theorem 3.2.4.1: the coarse spectral expansion of the Jacquet–Rallis trace formula for Schwartz functions
items.statement: Let T ∈ a^+_{n+1}. (1) f ↦ Σ_χ ∫_{[H]}∫_{[G′]} |K^T_{f,χ}(h, g′)| dg′ dh is finite and a continuous seminorm on 𝒮(G(A)). (2) I^T_χ(f) = ∫_{[H]}∫_{[G′]} K^T_{f,χ}(h, g′)η_{G′}(g′) dg′ dh is an exponential-polynomial in T whose purely polynomial part is a constant I_χ(f). (3) The distributions I_χ are continuous, left H(A)-invariant and right (G′(A), η_{G′})-equivariant. (4) I(f) = Σ_χ I_χ(f) converges absolutely and defines a continuous distribution — the coarse spectral expansion of Zydor's Jacquet–Rallis trace formula for G.
items.note: Extends Zydor, Crelle 2020, Theorems 0.1, 3.1, 3.7 and 3.9 from C_c^∞ to 𝒮(G(A)); (1) comes from Theorem 3.3.7.1 and Proposition 3.3.5.1, (2)–(4) as in Zydor. Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu's quasi-cuspidal expansions (their Props. 4.1–4.2) are the special case where only cuspidal χ contribute.

items.name: The Ichino–Yamana truncation operator Λ^T_r
items.statement: For a function φ on [G] = [G_n] × [G_{n+1}] and T ∈ a_{n+1}, (Λ^T_rφ)(h) = Σ_{P∈F_RS} ε^G_P Σ_{δ∈P_H(F)∖H(F)} τ̂_{P_{n+1}}(H_{P_{n+1}}(δh) − T_{P_{n+1}}) φ_{G_n×P_{n+1}}(δh) on [H], with φ_{G_n×P_{n+1}} the constant term along G_n × P_{n+1}. Proposition 3.3.2.1 (Ichino–Yamana, Lemma 2.4): for N, N′ and K_0 there are r and X_i ∈ 𝒰(𝔤_ℂ) of degree ≤ r with |(Λ^T_rφ)(h)| ≤ ‖h‖^{−N}_H Σ_i sup_x ‖x‖^{−N′}_G |(R(X_i)φ)(x)| for φ ∈ C^r(G(F)∖G(A)/K_0): it turns uniform moderate growth into rapid decay on [H].
items.note: Ichino–Yamana, Compositio 151 (2015), a variant of Arthur's Lemma 1.4 (Compositio 1980). Owned with the regularised Rankin–Selberg period it defines.

items.name: Propositions 3.3.2.2 and 3.3.3.1: the truncated kernel is rapidly decreasing and integrable
items.statement: For every N ≥ 0 there is a continuous seminorm ‖·‖_𝒮 on 𝒮(G(A)) with Σ_χ |Λ^T_rK_{f,χ}(h, g)| ≤ ‖f‖_𝒮‖h‖^{−N}_H‖g‖^{−N}_G on [H] × [G]; hence f ↦ Σ_χ ∫_{[H]×[G′]} |Λ^T_rK_{f,χ}(h, g′)| dh dg′ is a convergent continuous seminorm.
items.note: From Lemma 2.10.1.1 with w = ‖·‖_G and Proposition 3.3.2.1.

items.name: Arthur's characteristic function F^{G_{n+1}}(·, T)
items.statement: For T sufficiently positive, F^{G_{n+1}}(x, T) is the characteristic function of the x ∈ G_{n+1}(A) with δx ∈ 𝔰_{G_{n+1}} and ⟨ϖ, H_0(δx) − T⟩ ≤ 0 for all ϖ ∈ Δ̂_{B_{n+1}} for some δ ∈ G_{n+1}(F); it descends to the characteristic function of a compact subset of Z_{n+1}(A)G_{n+1}(F)∖G_{n+1}(A); F^{G′_{n+1}} is defined relative to G′_{n+1}.
items.note: Arthur, Duke 1978, §6; part of the truncation layer AS.3.

items.name: Proposition 3.3.5.1 and the second modified kernel κ^T_{f,χ}
items.statement: The maps f ↦ Σ_χ ∫_{[H]×[G′]} F^{G_{n+1}}(h, T)|K_{f,χ}(h, g′)| and f ↦ Σ_χ ∫_{[H]×[G′]} F^{G′_{n+1}}(g′_n, T)|K_{f,χ}(h, g′)| are convergent continuous seminorms on 𝒮(G(A)). κ^T_{f,χ}(h, g′) = Σ_{P∈F_RS} ε^G_P Σ_{γ∈P_H(F)∖H(F), δ∈P′(F)∖G′(F)} τ̂_{P_{n+1}}(H_{P_{n+1}}(γh) − T_{P_{n+1}})K_{f,P,χ}(γh, δg′), absolutely convergent (the sum over γ is finite).
items.note: Uses (3.3.2.3) and the compactness of the supports of F(·, T) on [H] and [G′_n].

items.name: Theorem 3.3.7.1: the modified kernels are asymptotic to Arthur-truncated kernels
items.statement: (1) For every N > 0 there is a continuous seminorm ‖·‖_{𝒮,N} on 𝒮(G(A)) with Σ_χ |K^T_{f,χ}(h, g′) − F^{G′_{n+1}}(g′_n, T)K_{f,χ}(h, g′)| ≤ e^{−N‖T‖}‖h‖^{−N}_H‖g′‖^{−N}_{G′}‖f‖_{𝒮,N} for T sufficiently positive, hence the integrated bound Σ_χ ∫ |…| ≤ e^{−N‖T‖}‖f‖_{𝒮,N}. (2) The same with κ^T_{f,χ}(h, g′) − F^{G_{n+1}}(h, T)K_{f,χ}(h, g′).
items.note: Proved by writing K^T and F·K as kernels of the separately continuous operators L^T_f, P^T_f: 𝒯^0([H]) ⊗ 𝒯^0([G′_{n+1}]) → 𝒮_0([G′_n]) built from Propositions 3.4.2.1, 3.4.3.1 and Theorem 3.5.1.1 (3.6.1.1)–(3.6.2.5); part (2) is 'similar and left to the reader'.

items.name: Proposition 3.3.8.1 and Lemma 3.7.5.1: the kernel κ^T gives the same I_χ
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛(G): (1) i^T_χ(f) = ∫_{[H]×[G′]} κ^T_{f,χ}(h, g′)η_{G′}(g′) converges for T sufficiently positive; (2) T ↦ i^T_χ(f) is an exponential-polynomial with purely polynomial part the constant I_χ(f). Lemma 3.7.5.1: i^T_χ(f) = Σ_{Q∈F_RS} c_Q e^{ρ_Q(T)} I^{M_Q,T}_χ(f̃_Q), where ρ_Q = ρ_{Q_{n+1}} − ρ_{Q_n}, I^{M_Q,T}_χ are Zydor's Levi distributions (3.7.4.2) (exponential-polynomials with exponents in {ρ_P − ρ_Q}), f̃_Q(m) = e^{−⟨ρ_Q,H_{Q_{n+1}}(m_n)⟩}p_Q(H_{Q_{n+1}}(m_n))f_Q(m) with f_Q the (K_H × K′, η)-averaged constant term, p_Q(X) = ∫_{a^{G_{n+1}}_{Q_{n+1}}} e^{ρ_Q(H)}Γ′_{Q_{n+1}}(H, X) dH (Arthur's Γ′ functions) and c_Q the Jacobian of a_{Q,H} ≅ a^{G_{n+1}}_{Q_{n+1}}.
items.note: Arthur's Γ′-functions are from 'The trace formula in invariant form' (Ann. of Math. 1981, §2), whose (G,M)-family arguments AS.6 plans; the exponential-polynomial property of p_Q is Zydor, Crelle 2020, Lemme 3.5.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.9.1: three truncated expressions for I_χ (= Theorem 1.2.4.1)
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛(G), f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)) and T sufficiently positive, let (I^T_χ, P^T_χ) be one of: (I^T_χ(f), ∫_{[H]×[G′]} F^{G′_{n+1}}(g′_n, T)K_χ(h, g′)η_{G′}(g′)); (i^T_χ(f), ∫ F^{G_{n+1}}(h, T)K_χ(h, g′)η_{G′}(g′)); (i^T_χ(f), ∫_{[H]×[G′]} Λ^T_rK_χ(h, g′)η_{G′}(g′)). (1) These integrals converge absolutely and T ↦ P^T_χ(f) is asymptotic to an exponential-polynomial whose constant term is I_χ(f); (2) for every N there is a continuous seminorm with |I^T_χ(f) − P^T_χ(f)| ≤ ‖f‖_{𝒮,N}e^{−N‖T‖}.
items.note: The third asymptotic reduces to ∫∫|Λ^T_rK_χ − F^{G_{n+1}}(h, T)K_χ| ≤ ‖f‖e^{−N‖T‖}, which 'can be proved as in Ichino–Yamana, proof of Prop. 3.8, and is left to the reader' — a proof obligation for the design.

items.name: The spaces 𝒯_{F_RS}([G]) and 𝒯^Δ_{F_RS}([G]) of compatible families
items.statement: For 𝐆 ∈ {G′_n, G′_{n+1}, G_n, G_{n+1}, H, G}, 𝒯_{F_RS}(𝐆) is the space of families (_Pφ)_{P∈F_RS} ∈ ∏ 𝒯([𝐆]_𝐏) with _Pφ − (_Qφ)_𝐏 ∈ 𝒮_{θ^Q_P}([𝐆]_𝐏) for P ⊂ Q, where θ^Q_P is d^{Q′_{n+1}}_{P′_{n+1}}, d^{Q_{n+1}}_{P_{n+1}} or d^Q_P according to 𝐆 (equivalently |R(X)(_Pφ − _Qφ)(g)| ≪ ‖g‖^{N_0}θ^Q_P(g)^{−r}); 𝒯^Δ_{F_RS}([G]) uses 𝒮_{Δ_P}([G]_P) and 𝒮_{d^{Q,Δ}_P}. Both are LF spaces, 𝒯_{F_RS}([H]) = 𝒯_{F_RS}([G_n]), and every family decomposes absolutely summably along cuspidal data (3.4.2.4).
items.note: Auxiliary spaces for the proof of Theorem 3.3.7.1.

items.name: Propositions 3.4.2.1 and 3.4.3.1: operations on compatible families
items.statement: (1) For φ ∈ 𝒯^0([H]) and f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)), (R(f)φ_{P_H})_{P∈F_RS} ∈ 𝒯^Δ_{F_RS}([G]); (2) for 𝐆 ∈ {G_{n+1}, G}, φ ∈ 𝒯^0([𝐆′]) gives (R(f)φ_{𝐏′}) ∈ 𝒯_{F_RS}([𝐆]); (3) restriction maps 𝒯_{F_RS}([G_n]) → 𝒯_{F_RS}([G′_n]) and 𝒯_{F_RS}([G]) → 𝒯_{F_RS}([H]); (4) products (g_n, g_{n+1}) ↦ _Pφ(g) _Pψ(g_{n+1}) of families in 𝒯^Δ_{F_RS}([G]) and 𝒯_{F_RS}([G_{n+1}]) lie in 𝒯^Δ_{F_RS}([G]). Proposition 3.4.3.1: for (_Pφ) ∈ 𝒯^Δ_{F_RS}([G]) and ψ ∈ 𝒯^0([G′_{n+1}]), the family P ↦ ⟨_Pφ, ψ_{P′_{n+1}}⟩(g_n) = ∫_{[G_{n+1}]_{P_{n+1}}} _Pφ(g_n, g_{n+1})ψ_{P′_{n+1}}(g_{n+1}) lies in 𝒯_{F_RS}([G_n]).
items.note: Proofs by Lemma 2.4.4.1 and the characterisations (3.4.1.1), (3.4.1.3).

items.name: Theorem 3.5.1.1: the relative truncation operator Λ^{T,𝐆} is asymptotic to F(·, T)
items.statement: For 𝐆 ∈ {H, G′_n, G_n} and φ = (_Pφ) ∈ 𝒯_{F_RS}([𝐆]): Λ^{T,𝐆}φ(g) = Σ_{P∈F_RS} ε^G_P Σ_{δ∈𝐏(F)∖𝐆(F)} τ̂_{P_{n+1}}(H_{P_{n+1}}(δg) − T_{P_{n+1}}) _Pφ(δg), and Π^{T,𝐆}φ = F^{G′_{n+1}}(·, T) _Gφ (𝐆 = G′_n) or F^{G_{n+1}}(·, T) _Gφ. For T sufficiently positive Λ^{T,𝐆}φ ∈ 𝒮_0([𝐆]), and for all c, N > 0 there is a continuous seminorm with ‖Λ^{T,𝐆}φ − Π^{T,𝐆}φ‖_{∞,N} ≤ e^{−c‖T‖}‖φ‖_{F_RS,c,N}. Lemma 3.5.1.2: e^{‖T‖} ≪ (min_α d_{P_{n+1},α}(g))^r and ‖g‖_{P_n} ≪ (max_α d_{P_{n+1},α}(g))^r, α ∈ Δ^{Q_{n+1}}_0 ∖ Δ^{P_{n+1}}_0, on the support of F^{P_{n+1}}(g, T)σ^{Q_{n+1}}_{P_{n+1}}(H_{P_{n+1}}(g) − T_{P_{n+1}}).
items.note: Uses Zydor's Lemme 2.1 and Prop. 2.8 and Arthur's analysis (Duke 1978, §§6–7, Cor. 6.2, (7.7)); the cases H and G_n reduce to G′_n by change of base field.

items.name: Flicker–Rallis periods, distinction and the Asai dichotomy
items.statement: For a cuspidal π of G_n(A) = GL_n(A_E) with central character trivial on A^∞_{G_n}, π* its conjugate dual: π is G′_n-distinguished ((G′_n, η)-distinguished) if φ ↦ ∫_{[G′_n]_0} φ(h) dh (∫_{[G′_n]_0} φ(h)η(det h) dh) is non-zero on 𝒜_π(G_n). π is conjugate self-dual iff it is G′_n-distinguished or (G′_n, η)-distinguished, and not both; distinction corresponds to a pole at s = 1 of an Asai L-function (Flicker): condition 1 of §1.1.3 (a pole of L(s, Π_i, As^{(−1)^{n+1}})) is equivalent to Π_i being (GL_{n_i,F}, η^{n+1})-distinguished.
items.note: Flicker, Twisted tensors and Euler products (Bull. SMF 1988): the factorisation L(s, π × π^c) = L(s, π, As^+)L(s, π, As^−) and the residue of the Asai integral as the Flicker–Rallis period.

items.name: Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski Flicker–Rallis intertwining periods J(φ) and J_Q(φ, λ)
items.statement: For P = MN_P standard, π = σ_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ σ_r cuspidal on M = G_{n_1} × ⋯ × G_{n_r} with central character trivial on A^∞_M, P′ = P ∩ G′ = M′N_{P′}: J(φ) = ∫_{A^∞_{M′}M′(F)N_{P′}(A)∖G′(A)} φ(g) dg, a G′(A)-invariant continuous form on 𝒜_{P,π}(G), non-zero iff each σ_i is G′_{n_i}-distinguished (then π = π*). For Q ∈ 𝒫(M) with Q′ = wQw^{−1} standard and w ∈ W(P; Q′): J_Q(φ, λ) = J(M(w, λ)φ), meromorphic in λ ∈ a^{G,*}_{P,ℂ}. The η-twisted variant J_η(φ) = ∫ φ(g)η_{G′}(g) dg for G = G_n × G_{n+1} (5.1.2.1); π is (M′, η_{G′})-distinguished if J_η ≢ 0.
items.note: A special case of the intertwining periods of Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 1999, §VII), with a slightly different 𝒜_{P,π}(G).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.9.1: the relative characters J_{Q,π}(g, λ, f) form a (G, M)-family
items.statement: For φ, ψ ∈ 𝒜_{P,π}(G), B_Q(g, φ, ψ, λ) = E(g, φ, λ)·\overline{J_Q(ψ̄, −λ)} is holomorphic on an open ω_π ⊃ ia^{G,*}_P (the complement of hyperplanes) and continuous sesquilinear there; J_{Q,π}(g, λ, f) = Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} B_Q(g, I_P(λ, f)φ, φ, λ) is a continuous distribution on 𝒮(G(A)). The family (J_{Q,π}(g, λ, f))_{Q∈𝒫(M)} is a (G, M)-family in Arthur's sense: each is smooth on ia^{G,*}_M (holomorphic on ω_π) and J_{Q_1,π} = J_{Q_2,π} on ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ = 0 for adjacent Q_1, Q_2 with Δ_{Q_1} ∩ (−Δ_{Q_2}) = {α}.
items.note: Uses Lapid, JIMJ 2006, Lemma 8.1 (case 1), and Keys–Shahidi, Ann. Sci. ENS 1988, Prop. 6.3 (M(s_α, 0) = −1 when σ_i ≅ σ*_{i+1} ≅ σ_i); (G, M)-families themselves are AS.6.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.10.1: λ ↦ J_{Q,π}(g, λ, f) is Schwartz
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)), λ ↦ J_{Q,π}(g, λ, f) lies in 𝒮(ia^{G,*}_P), and f ↦ J_{Q,π}(g, ·, f) is continuous 𝒮(G(A)) → 𝒮(ia^{G,*}_P).
items.note: Sketched from Lapid's majorisation of Eisenstein series (JIMJ 2006, Prop. 6.1 and §7, extended to Schwartz functions as in Feigon–Lapid–Offen, Remark C.2), Lapid's bounds for normalising factors (Lemma 5.1) and Müller–Speh's bound on normalised intertwining operators (GAFA 2004, Prop. 4.2).

items.name: The Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski mixed truncation Λ^T_m and the truncated kernel K^0_χΛ^T_m
items.statement: For φ on [G_n], (Λ^T_mφ)(h) = Σ_P (−1)^{dim a^G_P} Σ_{δ∈P′(F)∖G′(F)} τ̂_P(H_P(δh) − T_P) φ_P(δh) on [G′_n] (sum over standard P, φ_P the constant term). Lemma 4.2.3.1: (K^0_χΛ^T_m)(x, y) = Σ_{B⊂P} |𝒫(M_P)|^{−1} ∫_{ia^{G,*}_P} Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,χ}} E(x, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ) \overline{Λ^T_mE(y, φ, λ)} dλ; Lemma 4.2.3.2: the corresponding absolute sum with R(X) is bounded by ‖L(X)f‖‖x‖^{N′}‖y‖^{−N}; Proposition 4.2.3.3: ∫_{[G′]_0} (K^0_χΛ^T_m)(x, y) dy = Σ_{B⊂P} |𝒫(M_P)|^{−1} ∫_{ia^{G,*}_P} Σ_φ E(x, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ) ∫_{[G′]_0} \overline{Λ^T_mE(y, φ, λ)} dy dλ.
items.note: Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski 1999; the rapid decay of Λ^T_m is a variant of Arthur's Lemma 1.4 (Compositio 1980) as in Lapid–Rogawski (Duke 2003, Lemma 8.2.1).

items.name: ∗-regular cuspidal data of G_n
items.statement: χ ∈ 𝔛(G_n) is ∗-regular if for every representative (M, π) and w ∈ W(M) with wπ ≅ π or wπ ≅ π*, w = 1; for π = σ_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ σ_r this means: for i ≠ j with n_i = n_j, σ_i ≠ σ_j and σ_i ≠ σ*_j. 𝔛*(G_n) denotes the ∗-regular data; for G = G_n × G_{n+1}, 𝔛*(G) = 𝔛*(G_n) × 𝔛*(G_{n+1}).
items.note: The data attached to (isobaric) Hermitian Arthur parameters.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.3.1: spectral expansion of the Flicker–Rallis period of the kernel
items.statement: Let f ∈ 𝒮(G_n(A)), χ ∈ 𝔛(G_n), g ∈ G_n(A). (1) ∫_{[G′]} K_χ(g, h) dh = ½ ∫_{[G′]_0} K^0_χ(g, h) dh, both absolutely convergent. (2) If χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n) with representative (M_P, π), then ∫_{[G′]} K_χ(g, h) dh = 2^{−dim a_P} J_{P,π}(g, f), where J_{P,π}(g, f) = J_{P,π}(g, 0, f); in particular it vanishes unless π is conjugate self-dual and M_{P′}-distinguished. The contribution is purely discrete (Remark 1.3.1.2), in contrast with the Arthur–Selberg trace formula.
items.note: The η-twisted version for G = G_n × G_{n+1} is used in §5; the proof avoids Lapid's contour shifting (JIMJ 2006) by truncating first.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.4.1: the mixed-truncation limit formula
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 4.3.3.1 (no regularity needed), lim_{T→+∞} ∫_{[G′]_0} (K^0_χΛ^T_m)(g, h) dh = 2∫_{[G′]} K_χ(g, h) dh, the limit taken as ⟨α, T⟩ → +∞ for all α ∈ Δ_B.
items.note: By a variant of Arthur, Canad. J. Math. 1985, Thm. 3.1 (cf. Ichino–Yamana, Prop. 3.8) and dominated convergence.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.6.1 and Lemma 4.3.6.2: the truncated Flicker–Rallis period of Eisenstein series
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n), P_1 ∈ 𝒫_χ and φ ∈ 𝒜_{P_1,χ}: ∫_{[G′]_0} Λ^T_mE(y, φ, λ) dy = 2^{−dim a^G_{P_1}} Σ_{Q∈𝒫(M_1)} J_Q(φ, λ)e^{⟨λ,T_Q⟩}/θ_Q(λ) for λ ∈ ia^{G,*}_{P_1} (Lemma 4.3.6.2); hence ∫_{[G′]_0} (K^0_χΛ^T_m)(g, h) dh = (2^{−dim a^G_P}/|𝒫(M_P)|) Σ_{P_1∈𝒫_χ} ∫_{ia^{G,*}_{P_1}} Σ_{Q∈𝒫(M_1)} J_{Q,χ}(g, λ, f)e^{−⟨λ,T_Q⟩}/θ_Q(−λ) dλ, with J_{Q,χ} = Σ_{w∈W(P,P_1)} J_{Q,wπ} (Proposition 4.3.6.1).
items.note: Lemma 4.3.6.2 rephrases Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski, Theorem 40, for ∗-regular data; its printed range λ ∈ ia^G_{P_1} means ia^{G,*}_{P_1} (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.7.1 and Lemma 4.3.7.2: the limit is discrete
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n) represented by (M_P, π): lim_{T→+∞} ∫_{[G′]_0} (K^0_χΛ^T_m)(g, h) dh = 2^{−dim a^G_P} J_{P,π}(g, f), J_{P,π}(g, f) = J_{P,π}(g, 0, f). Lemma 4.3.7.2 (Lapid): J_{P_1,wπ}(g, 0, f) = J_{P,π}(g, 0, f) for w ∈ W(P, P_1).
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed integral over [G′] is over [G′]_0 (sourceIssues E3). Uses Lapid's limit lemma for (G, M)-families of Schwartz functions (Clay Math. Proc. 13 (2011), Lemma 8), |𝒫(M_P)| = Σ_{P_1∈𝒫_χ} |W(P, P_1)|, the functional equation of Eisenstein series and Lapid 2006, Lemma 8.1.

items.name: Relevant and ∗-regular cuspidal data of G = G_n × G_{n+1}
items.statement: χ ∈ 𝔛(G) with representative (M, π) is relevant if π is (M′, η_{G′})-distinguished (J_η ≢ 0); ∗-regular if χ ∈ 𝔛*(G) = 𝔛*(G_n) × 𝔛*(G_{n+1}). A relevant regular datum is ∗-regular, and χ is regular and relevant exactly when Π = Ind^G_P(π) is a Hermitian Arthur parameter.
items.note: The spectral data that the Jacquet–Rallis comparison matches with unitary groups.

items.name: Proposition 5.1.4.1: the regularised Rankin–Selberg period of Eisenstein series
items.statement: Let Q ⊂ G be parabolic, π cuspidal on M_Q and (M_{Q′}, η_{G′})-distinguished, φ ∈ 𝒜_{Q,π}(G). For λ ∈ a^{G,*}_Q regular for E(g, φ, λ), I(φ, λ) = ∫_{[H]} Λ^T_rE(h, φ, λ) dh converges and does not depend on T ∈ a^+_{n+1}; it is Ichino–Yamana's regularised Rankin–Selberg period of E(φ, λ) (Remark 5.1.4.2).
items.note: Independence of T: by Ichino–Yamana's Lemma 2.2 the difference is a sum over proper P ∈ F_RS whose terms contain ∫_{[G_{d_1}]^1} E(g, φ_1, λ_1)Λ^TE(g, φ_2, λ_2), which vanishes by Arthur's inner product formula (Duke 1982) because π_2 would be both (η_{d_1})^n- and (η_{d_1})^{n+1}-distinguished.

items.name: The relative characters I^T_{P,π} and I_{P,π}
items.statement: For P standard in G and π cuspidal on M_P: I^T_{P,π}(f) = Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} ∫_{[H]} Λ^T_rE(h, I_P(0, f)φ, 0) dh · \overline{J_η(φ)}; by Proposition 5.1.4.1 it equals I_{P,π}(f) = Σ_φ I(I_P(0, f)φ, 0)\overline{J_η(φ)} if π is (M_{P′}, η_{G′})-distinguished and 0 otherwise. Proposition 5.1.5.1: for χ ∈ 𝔛*(G) with representative (P, π), f ↦ I^T_{P,π}(f) is a continuous linear form on 𝒮(G(A)) depending only on χ.
items.note: Built from the regularised Rankin–Selberg period and the Flicker–Rallis intertwining period; continuity by Proposition 2.8.4.1.

items.name: Theorem 5.2.1.1: the ∗-regular contribution is discrete (first proof, by truncation)
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G) represented by (M, π), P standard: I_χ = 2^{−dim a_P} I_{P,π}; in particular I_χ = 0 unless χ is relevant. Proposition 5.2.1.2: for T ∈ a^+_{n+1}, ∫_{[H]}∫_{[G′]} Λ^T_rK_χ(x, y)η_{G′}(y) dx dy = 2^{−dim a_P} I_{P,π}(f), independently of T.
items.locator: Theorem 5.2.1.1 (= Theorem 1.3.2.1), Proposition 5.2.1.2, Lemmas 5.2.2.1 and 5.2.2.3, pp. 280–282
items.note: From Theorem 4.3.3.1 (η-twisted, for G_n and G_{n+1}), the commutation of Λ^T_r with the [G′]-integral and the basis sum (Lemmas 5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.3), and Theorem 3.3.9.1 for the constant term in T.

items.name: Mirabolic subgroups, generic characters and Whittaker functions of moderate-growth functions
items.statement: w_n is the antidiagonal permutation matrix, e_n = (0, …, 0, 1), P_n = G_{n−1}U_n and P′_n = P_n ∩ G′_n the mirabolic subgroups (stabilisers of e_n for the right action), G_m ⊂ G_n in the upper left corner. For φ ∈ 𝒮(A^n), φ̂(x) = ∫ φ(y)ψ′(Σx_iy_i) dy with self-dual measure. Fix τ ∈ E^× with τ^c = −τ and ψ(z) = ψ′(Tr_{E/F}(τz)); ψ_n(u) = ψ((−1)^n Σ_{i=1}^{n−1} u_{i,i+1}) is a generic character of [N_n], trivial on N′_n(A). For f ∈ 𝒯([G_n]), W_f(g) = ∫_{[N_n]} f(ug)ψ_n(u)^{−1} du; for f ∈ 𝒞([G_n]) and Π as in Theorem 2.9.8.1, W_{f,Π} = W_{f_Π} ∈ W(Π, ψ_n).
items.note: The sign (−1)^n is the convention matching §7.

items.name: The Flicker–Rallis zeta integral Z^FR_ψ(s, f, φ)
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒯([G_n]), φ ∈ 𝒮(A^n) and s ∈ ℂ: Z^FR_ψ(s, f, φ) = ∫_{N′_n(A)∖G′_n(A)} W_f(h)φ(e_nh)|det h|^s dh, where it converges absolutely; for cusp forms this is Flicker's integral representation of the Asai L-function.
items.note: Flicker 1988, extended to non-cuspidal f of uniform moderate growth.

items.name: The Asai L-function of an induced representation and its analytic properties
items.statement: For Π = Ind^{G_n(A)}_{P(A)}(π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ π_k): Shahidi's completed Asai L-function (Shahidi 1990; Goldberg 1994) factors as L(s, Π, As) = ∏_i L(s, π_i, As) ∏_{i<j} L(s, π_i × π^c_j), independently of the order. It has meromorphic continuation and functional equation with global ε-factor (Shahidi, Ann. of Math. 1990, Thm. 3.5(4)); L(s, π_i, As) has at most a simple pole at s = 1 (Flicker), and s ↦ (s − 1)L^{S_0}(s, π_i, As) (pole) or L^{S_0}(s, π_i, As) is holomorphic of finite order in vertical strips of ℋ_{>0} (Finis–Lapid, Lemma 5.2). For χ ∗-regular, L(s, Π, As) has a pole of order at most k at s = 1, of order exactly k iff every L(s, π_i, As) has a pole; χ is then called distinguished, equivalently π is M_{P′}-distinguished (Flicker).
items.note: The Langlands–Shahidi Asai L-function is not planned; AL.4 plans only the unramified Euler factors. The Rankin–Selberg factors L(s, π_i × π^c_j) are entire and non-vanishing at s = 1 for ∗-regular χ (separate item).

items.name: Rankin–Selberg analytic inputs for GL_n × GL_m
items.statement: For cuspidal π, π′ of GL_n(A_E), GL_m(A_E) with π′ ≄ π^∨ ⊗ |det|^{it}: L(s, π × π′) is entire, bounded in vertical strips (Cogdell, ICTP notes 2008, Thm. 4.1; Gelbart–Shahidi) and non-vanishing at s = 1 (Jacquet–Shalika 1981; Shahidi 1981); for π′ = π^∨ it has a simple pole at s = 1. The local Rankin–Selberg and Asai L-factors of unitary cuspidal components satisfy the Jacquet–Shalika bound, so Q(s)L_v(s) is holomorphic and bounded in vertical strips of ℋ_{>0} after multiplying by a polynomial Q with roots in ℋ_{]0,1[}.
items.note: These GL_n statements are the analytic part of AL.3 ('state analytic nonvanishing results only in their proved regions'); PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 routes Gelbart–Shahidi boundedness and PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 strong multiplicity one to the same source.

items.name: Strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations and Ramakrishnan's refinement
items.statement: Two isobaric sums of cuspidal automorphic representations of general linear groups whose local components are isomorphic at almost all places are equal (Jacquet–Shalika). Ramakrishnan (A theorem on GL(n) à la Tchebotarev, arXiv:1806.08429): for a finite Galois extension K/F, an isobaric automorphic representation of GL_n(A_K) is determined by its local components at the places of K of degree one over F. For K = E this identifies a weak base change (defined by the split places) with a strong one and lets the Satake parameters at split places single out Π.
items.locator: Remark 1.1.4.1 and proof of Proposition 10.1.6.1, pp. 185 and 321
items.note: Jacquet–Shalika's form coalesces with PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18's source route to AL.3; Ramakrishnan's theorem (via Rankin–Selberg theory, the Luo–Rudnick–Sarnak bound and class field theory) is also used by Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu.

items.name: The Flicker functional β_n on W(Π, ψ_n)
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n) distinguished and W ∈ W(Π, ψ_n): β_{n,S}(W) = ∫_{N′_n(F_S)∖P′_n(F_S)} W(p_S) dp_S, convergent by Beuzart-Plessis (Asai paper, Prop. 2.6.1, Lemma 3.3.1) and the Jacquet–Shalika bound; β_n(W) = (Δ^{S,*}_{G′_n})^{−1}L^{S,*}(1, Π, As)β_{n,S}(W), independent of S large (Flicker, Prop. 3, and (2.3.2.3)), where L^{S,*}(1, ·) is the leading Laurent coefficient at s = 1. For G = G_n × G_{n+1}: β_η(W) = (Δ^{S,*}_{G′})^{−1}L^{S,*}(1, Π, As_G)∫_{N′(F_S)∖𝒫′(F_S)} W(p_S)η_{G′}(p_S) dp_S with L(s, Π, As_G) = L(s, Π_n, As^{(−1)^{n+1}})L(s, Π_{n+1}, As^{(−1)^n}).
items.note: The mirabolic integral realises the Flicker–Rallis period on the Whittaker model.

items.name: Local Asai zeta integrals: continuation, functional equation and the unramified computation
items.statement: For S a finite set of places and W_S ∈ W(Π_S, ψ_{n,S}), φ_S ∈ 𝒮(F^n_S): Z^FR_ψ(s, W_S, φ_S) = ∫_{N′_n(F_S)∖G′_n(F_S)} W_S(h)φ_S(e_nh)|det h|^s dh continues meromorphically to ℂ with Z^FR_{ψ^{−1}}(1 − s, W̃_S, φ̂_S)/L_S(1 − s, Π^∨, As) = ε(s, Π, As)Z^FR_ψ(s, W_S, φ_S)/L_S(s, Π, As), W̃(g) = W(w_n{}^tg^{−1}) (Beuzart-Plessis, Thm. 3.5.1), with the quotients entire of finite order (Thm. 3.5.2); at unramified places the integral of the normalised spherical vector and 1_{O^n} is L_v(s, Π_v, As) (Flicker, Prop. 3), giving Z^FR_ψ(s, f, φ) = (Δ^{S,*}_{G′_n})^{−1}L(s, Π, As)Z^FR_ψ(s, W_S, φ_S)/L_S(s, Π, As) (6.3.0.6).
items.note: Beuzart-Plessis, Archimedean theory and ε-factors for the Asai Rankin–Selberg integrals (Simons Symposia 2021); the archimedean theory is not planned.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.5.1(1): convergence of Flicker–Rallis zeta integrals of moderate-growth functions
items.statement: For N ≥ 0 there is c_N > 0 such that for f ∈ 𝒯_N([G_n]) and φ ∈ 𝒮(A^n), Z^FR_ψ(s, f, φ) converges absolutely for s ∈ ℋ_{>c_N}, is holomorphic and bounded in vertical strips there, and is a separately continuous bilinear form on 𝒯_N([G_n]) × 𝒮(A^n) for each such s.
items.note: By Lemma 2.6.1.1(2) and Lemma 2.6.2.1.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.5.1(2): the residue of the Flicker–Rallis zeta integral for ∗-regular data
items.statement: Let χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n) with representative (M_P, π), M_P = G_{n_1} × ⋯ × G_{n_k}, and ⁰f(g) = ∫_{A^∞_{G_n}} f(ag) da. For f ∈ 𝒞_χ([G_n]) and φ ∈ 𝒮(A^n), s ↦ (s − 1)Z^FR_ψ(s, ⁰f, φ) continues analytically to ℋ_{>1} with a limit at s = 1, and Z^{FR,*}_ψ(1, ⁰f, φ) = lim_{s→1+}(s − 1)Z^FR_ψ(s, ⁰f, φ) = 2^{1−k}φ̂(0)β_n(W_{f,Π}) if χ is distinguished, and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Proof: Lapid's expansion ⁰f = ∫_{ia*_{M,0}} f_x dx (6.3.0.2), the local theory, and the vector-valued Phragmén–Lindelöf principle (Corollary A.0.11.1) applied to P(s, x)Z^FR(s, f_x, φ); then Beuzart-Plessis (Invent. 2021) Lemma 3.1.1, Prop. 3.1.2 and Lemma 2.16.3 for the limit. The parameter space written 𝒜_0 is ia*_{M,0} (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: The Epstein–Eisenstein series on G′_n
items.statement: For φ ∈ 𝒮(A^n): E(h, φ, s) = ∫_{A^∞_{G′_n}} Σ_{γ∈P′_n(F)∖G′_n(F)} φ(e_nγah)|det(ah)|^s da, absolutely convergent for Re s > 1, continuing meromorphically to a function valued in 𝒯([G′_n]) with simple poles at s = 0, 1 and residues φ(0), φ̂(0) (Jacquet–Shalika, Amer. J. Math. 1981, Lemma 4.2).
items.note: Its pairing with ⁰f realises the Flicker–Rallis period as a residue.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.0.1 and Proposition 6.4.0.2: partial Whittaker unfolding of the Flicker–Rallis integral
items.statement: For 1 ≤ r ≤ n let N_{r,n} be the unipotent radical of the standard parabolic with Levi G_r × (G_1)^{n−r}, ⁰f_{N_{r,n},ψ} the ψ_n-coefficient along it and Z^FR_r(s, ⁰f, φ) = ∫_{P′_r(F)N′_{r,n}(A)∖G′_n(A)} ⁰f_{N_{r,n},ψ}(h)φ(e_nh)|det h|^s dh (Z^FR_1 = Z^FR_ψ, Z^FR_n(s, ⁰f, φ) = ∫_{[G′_n]_0} ⁰f(h)E(h, φ, s)dh). Lemma 6.4.0.1: Z^FR_r converges for Re s > c_r. Proposition 6.4.0.2: for f ∈ 𝒮_χ([G_n]), χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n), each s ↦ (s − 1)Z^FR_r(s, ⁰f, φ) extends holomorphically to Re s > 1 with a limit at s = 1, and these limits are equal for all r; the correction F_r(s) between consecutive r is holomorphic on Re s > 1 − r/n.
items.note: The correction terms are expressed through P_{G′_r} ⊗̂ Z^FR_{n−r} applied to 𝒞_{χ_M} constant terms (Corollary 2.9.7.2); ∗-regularity passes to the factor χ_2.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.6.1: the Flicker–Rallis period on 𝒞([G_n]) is a residue
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n), P_{G′_n}: f ↦ ∫_{[G′_n]} f(h) dh is well defined and continuous on 𝒞([G_n]), and for f ∈ 𝒮_χ([G_n]) and φ ∈ 𝒮(A^n): φ̂(0)P_{G′_n}(f) = ½ Z^{FR,*}_ψ(1, ⁰f, φ).
items.note: Continuity from Ξ^{G_n}(h) ≪ Ξ^{G′_n}(h)² and (2.4.5.24); the factor ½ from the measures on A^∞_{G_n} and A^∞_{G′_n}.

items.name: Corollary 6.2.7.1: the Flicker–Rallis period of a Schwartz function supported on a ∗-regular datum (= Theorem 1.3.3.1)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ 𝔛*(G_n) be represented by (M_P, π) and Π = Ind^{G_n(A)}_{P(A)}(π). For every f ∈ 𝒮_χ([G_n]): P_{G′_n}(f) = 2^{−dim A_P}β_n(W_{f,Π}) if χ is distinguished, and 0 otherwise. With the η-twist, for G = G_n × G_{n+1}: P_{G′,η}(φ) = ∫_{[G′]} φ(g′)η_{G′}(g′) dg′ = 2^{−dim A_M}β_η(W_{φ_0}) for φ ∈ 𝒮_χ([G]).
items.note: Combines Theorems 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.6.1.

items.name: The Rankin–Selberg zeta integral Z^RS_ψ(s, f) of moderate-growth functions
items.statement: For G = G_n × G_{n+1}, H = G_n diagonal, ψ_N = ψ_n ⊠ ψ_{n+1} (trivial on [N_H]) and f ∈ 𝒯([G]): W_f(g) = ∫_{[N]} f(ug)ψ_N(u)^{−1} du and Z^RS_ψ(s, f) = ∫_{N_H(A)∖H(A)} W_f(h)|det h|^s_E dh where absolutely convergent. Lemma 7.1.1.1: for N ≥ 0 there is c_N with Z^RS_ψ(s, f) absolutely convergent for f ∈ 𝒯_N([G]) and s ∈ ℋ_{>c_N}, continuous in f and holomorphic and bounded in vertical strips in s.
items.note: Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika's integral with the center shifted by ½ relative to the introduction's normalisation.

items.name: H-regular cuspidal data
items.statement: χ ∈ 𝔛(G) represented by (M_P, π), π_n = π_{n,1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ π_{n,k}, π_{n+1} = π_{n+1,1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ π_{n+1,r}, is H-regular if π_{n,i} ≠ π^∨_{n+1,j} for all i, j (7.1.2.1). Relevant data are H-regular, by the dichotomy of §4.1.2.
items.note: The condition that kills the extra terms in the Rankin–Selberg unfolding.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.0.2: the partial Rankin–Selberg unfolding for H-regular data
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒮_χ([G]), χ H-regular, and 1 ≤ r ≤ n, with N^G_r = N_{r,n} × N_{r,n+1} and Z^RS_r(s, f) = ∫_{𝒫_r(F)N^H_r(A)∖H(A)} f_{N^G_r,ψ}(h)|det h|^s_E dh (convergent for Re s > c_r, Lemma 7.2.0.1) and Z^RS_{n+1}(s, f) = ∫_{[H]} f(h)|det h|^s_E dh: Z^RS_{r+1}(s, f) = Z^RS_r(s, f) for Re s large. The correction terms F_r(s) = ∫_K (P_{G_{Δ_r}} ⊗̂ Z^RS_{n−r}(s + 2rα_r(s)))(f_{𝒫_r,k,s}) dk, α_r(s) = (2s + 1)/(4n − 4r + 2), vanish because the diagonal period of G_r × G_r kills 𝒞_{χ_1}([G_r × G_r]) when χ″_1 ≠ (χ′_1)^∨.
items.note: Mimics the Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika unfolding for non-cuspidal functions.

items.name: Theorem 7.1.3.1: canonical extension of the Rankin–Selberg period (= Theorem 1.3.3.2)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ 𝔛(G) be H-regular. (1) For every f ∈ 𝒯_χ([G]), s ↦ Z^RS_ψ(s, f) extends from a right half-plane to an entire function. (2) The restriction of P_H: f ↦ ∫_{[H]} f(h) dh to 𝒮_χ([G]) extends by continuity to 𝒯_χ([G]), and P_H(f) = Z^RS_ψ(0, f) for every f ∈ 𝒯_χ([G]) (7.1.3.2).
items.note: Z^RS_ψ(s, f) = ∫_{[H]} f(h)|det h|^s dh for f ∈ 𝒮_χ([G]) gives an entire function with Z^RS_ψ(−s, f̃) = Z^RS_ψ(s, f), f̃(g) = f(^tg^{−1}); Corollary A.0.11.2 (vector-valued Phragmén–Lindelöf) extends it to 𝒯_χ. Written ∫* in the introduction.

items.name: The linear forms λ, β_η and the Whittaker inner product ⟨·,·⟩_Whitt on W(Π, ψ_N)
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G) represented by (M_P, π), Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} = Ind^G_P(π) is generic; W_φ = W_{E(φ)} ∈ W(Π, ψ_N) for φ ∈ Π. λ(W) = Z^RS(0, W), where Z^RS(s, W) = ∫_{N_H(A)∖H(A)} W(h)|det h|^s_{A_E} dh converges for Re s ≫ 0 and continues meromorphically with no pole at s = 0 (Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika; Jacquet 2009); β_η as in §6.2.4; ⟨W, W⟩_Whitt = (Δ^{S,*}_G)^{−1}L^{S,*}(1, Π, Ad)∫_{N(F_S)∖𝒫(F_S)} |W(p_S)|² dp_S with L(s, Π, Ad) = L(s, Π_n × Π^∨_n)L(s, Π_{n+1} × Π^∨_{n+1}), independent of S large (Flicker; Jacquet–Shalika) and G(A)-invariant (Bernstein 1984; Baruch 2003).
items.note: 𝒫 = 𝒫_n × 𝒫_{n+1} is the product of mirabolic subgroups; the global Rankin–Selberg theory for cuspidal data is AL.3, the Whittaker functional of a non-cuspidal Eisenstein series is new here.

items.name: Theorem 8.1.2.1 (Jacquet–Shalika, Shahidi, Lapid–Offen): the Petersson norm is the Whittaker norm
items.statement: For φ ∈ Π (Π induced from a regular cuspidal datum): ⟨φ, φ⟩_Pet = ⟨W_φ, W_φ⟩_Whitt.
items.note: Deduced from Jacquet–Shalika's residue formula for cusp forms on M_P (8.1.2.1) (see also Feigon–Lapid–Offen p. 265, W. Zhang JAMS 2014 Prop. 3.1), Feigon–Lapid–Offen Prop. A.2 for the Jacquet integral (8.1.2.2) and Shahidi's computation W^S(φ_{N_P,ψ}) = ∏ L^S(1, π_i × π^∨_j)W_φ (8.1.2.3).

items.name: The Whittaker relative character I_Π
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G), Π = Ind^G_P(π) and a K-basis ℬ_{P,π}: I_Π(f) = Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} λ(R(f)W_φ)\overline{β_η(W_φ)}/⟨W_φ, W_φ⟩_Whitt for f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)), convergent and independent of the basis (Proposition 2.8.4.1); by Theorem 8.1.2.1 the denominators are 1 for a Petersson-orthonormal basis, giving (1.3.1.1).
items.note: Following W. Zhang, JAMS 2014, §3.4.

items.name: Theorem 8.1.4.1: the ∗-regular contribution in Whittaker terms (= Theorem 1.3.1.1)
items.statement: Let f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)), χ ∈ 𝔛*(G) and K^1_{f,χ}(g) = ∫_{[H]} K_{f,χ}(h, g) dh, K^2_{f,χ}(g) = ∫_{[G′]} K_{f,χ}(g, g′)η_{G′}(g′) dg′. (1) If χ is not relevant, K^2_{f,χ} ≡ 0 and I_χ(f) = 0. (2) If χ is relevant, I_χ(f) = ∫_{[G′]} K^1_{f,χ}(g′)η_{G′}(g′) dg′ (absolutely convergent) and I_χ(f) = 2^{−dim A_P}I_Π(f). For relevant ∗-regular χ the exponential-polynomial T ↦ I^T_χ(f) is constant.
items.note: Second proof, by zeta integrals: K^2_{f,χ} = P_{G′_n} ⊗̂ P_{G′_{n+1}}(K̃_{f,χ}(g, ·)) = 2^{−dim A_P}Σ_φ E(R(f)φ)(g)\overline{β_η(W_φ)} (Corollary 6.2.7.1), then P*_H(E(φ)) = λ(W_φ) (Theorem 7.1.3.1) and Theorem 3.3.9.1 applied to (3.3.5.6).

items.name: Local setup: mirabolic Flicker functionals and Jacquet integrals
items.statement: For E/F an étale quadratic algebra over a local field, ψ(x) = ψ′(Tr(τx)), measures dx = ∏dx_{ij}/|det x|^n on GL_n(k), product measures on Levi subgroups, additive measures on unipotent subgroups, and the linear forms ∫_{R∖S} on (R, δ_Rδ_S^{−1})-equivariant functions. For ϕ ∈ C^∞(N_0∖𝒫, ψ): β(ϕ) = β_G(ϕ) = ∫_{N_{0,F}∖𝒫_F} ϕ(p) dp, and β_M for standard Levi M. For σ ∈ Π_gen(M) and P = MN, Ind^G_P(W(σ)) and the Jacquet integral W(g, ϕ) = ∫_{N_w} δ^σ_e(ϕ(w_M^{−1}u′g))ψ^{−1}(u′) du′, a Whittaker functional W_e(ϕ) = W(e, ϕ).
items.note: Normalisations follow Feigon–Lapid–Offen, Appendix A.

items.name: Theorem 9.1.7.1: local Flicker functional of a Jacquet integral
items.statement: Let σ ∈ Π_gen(M) be unitary and distinguished (admitting a non-zero continuous G_F-invariant form) and ϕ ∈ Ind^G_P(W(σ)). Then β_M is M_F-invariant, β_G(W(ϕ)) and β_M(ϕ(g)) converge absolutely (Flicker, Lemma 4; Beuzart-Plessis, Asai paper, Prop. 2.6.1), and β_G(W(ϕ)) = β′(ϕ) := ∫_{P_F∖G_F} β_M(ϕ(g)) dg (9.1.7.1)–(9.1.7.2), the integral making sense as δ_P|_{P_F} = δ²_{P_F}.
items.note: Split E: Baruch, Cor. 10.4, and Feigon–Lapid–Offen, Prop. A.2. p-adic E/F: uniqueness of G_F-invariant forms (Gelbart–Jacquet–Rogawski, Prop. 2). F = ℝ: the paper sketches the analogue via multiplicity one (Aizenbud–Gourevitch, Thm. 8.2.5) and a variant of Baruch's Theorem 10.4 for Z(𝔤)-finite P_F-invariant distributions on G/G_F, 'proved as in Baruch §9' — a proof obligation. Non-vanishing of β′ from Gelfand–Kazhdan, Jacquet 2010 Prop. 5, Kemarsky 2015.

items.name: Lemmas 9.1.7.3–9.1.7.7: the Fourier-transform chain for a maximal parabolic
items.statement: For P maximal of type (n_1, n_2), with the groups C_i, R_i, X_i, Y_i, V_i, V′_i, S_i, S′_i and the induced spaces 𝒜_i = Ind^𝒫_{S_i}(W(σ_2) ⊗ ψ_i): the partial Fourier transforms F′_i: L²(C_i, 𝒲(σ_2)) → L²(R_{i−1}, 𝒲(σ_2)) induce unitary equivalences B_i: 𝒜²_i → 𝒜²_{i−1} (Lemma 9.1.7.3) and B_{n_2+1}: 𝒜²_{n_2+1} → 𝒜²_{n_2} (Lemma 9.1.7.4); for ϕ supported on the big cell, with ϕ_n(p) = δ^1_eϕ(wp) and ϕ_{i−1} = B_i(ϕ_i), ϕ_{n_2} = W(ϕ) (Feigon–Lapid–Offen, A.3) and β′(ϕ) = β_n(ϕ_n) (Lemma 9.1.7.5), β_i(ϕ_i) = β_{i−1}(ϕ_{i−1}) (Lemma 9.1.7.6), β_{n_2+1}(ϕ_{n_2+1}) = β_G(W(ϕ)) (Lemma 9.1.7.7), where β_i(φ) = ∫_{S_{i,F}∖𝒫_F} β_{M′_2}(φ(p)) dp.
items.note: A twisted version of the local unfolding of Feigon–Lapid–Offen, Appendix A; the reduction from general P to maximal P uses the transitivity of Jacquet integrals.

items.name: Theorem 9.2.5.1: the Flicker–Rallis intertwining period equals β_η (= Theorem 1.3.2.3)
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛*(G) relevant, represented by (M, π), Π = Ind^{G(A)}_{P(A)}(π) and every φ ∈ Π: J_η(φ) = β_η(W_φ).
items.note: Same structure as Theorem 8.1.2.1, with W. Zhang's JAMS 2014 Prop. 3.2 replacing (8.1.2.1) and Theorem 9.1.7.1 replacing (8.1.2.2).

items.name: Ichino–Yamana: the regularised Rankin–Selberg period of an Eisenstein series is its Rankin–Selberg zeta value
items.statement: For φ in Π induced from an (M_{Q′}, η_{G′})-distinguished cuspidal datum: λ(W_φ) = Z^RS(0, W_φ) = I(φ, 0), the regularised period of Proposition 5.1.4.1 (Ichino–Yamana, Compositio 2015, Thm. 1.1); and I (equivalently λ) is non-zero iff L(½, Π) ≠ 0 (Ichino–Yamana, Cor. 5.7; Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika, Jacquet 2004).
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 9.2.5.2, p. 318, and §10.2.1, pp. 322–323
items.note: Cited theorems of Ichino–Yamana; their proofs are the natural sequel to Proposition 5.1.4.1 and Theorem 7.1.3.1.

items.name: Corollary 9.2.5.2: the two relative characters coincide (= Theorem 1.3.2.4)
items.statement: For χ relevant and ∗-regular: I_{P,π} = I_Π as distributions on 𝒮(G(A)).
items.note: From Theorem 8.1.2.1, Theorem 9.2.5.1 and Ichino–Yamana's Theorem 1.1. A direct comparison of the truncation proof (§5) with the zeta-integral proof (§8).

items.name: Relative characters of unitary groups J^h_σ and J^h_{𝔛_0}
items.statement: For h ∈ ℋ and σ ⊂ 𝒜_cusp(U_h) irreducible: J^h_σ(f) = Σ_φ 𝒫_h(π(f)φ)\overline{𝒫_h(φ)} for f ∈ 𝒮(U_h(A)), over a K_h-basis; for 𝔛_0 ⊂ 𝔛(U_h) of cuspidal data not coming from proper Levi subgroups, J^h_{𝔛_0}(f) = Σ_{χ∈𝔛_0} Σ_σ J^h_σ(f) over the constituents of L²_χ([U_h]), absolutely convergent (Beuzart-Plessis, JIMJ 2021, Prop. A.1.2).
items.note: The unitary-side relative characters of the Jacquet–Rallis comparison.

items.name: Unramified data: ℋ°, spherical Hecke algebras and the base-change homomorphism
items.statement: For V_{F,∞} ⊂ S_0 finite containing the places ramified in E, ℋ° ⊂ ℋ is the finite set of hermitian spaces with a self-dual O_{E_v}-lattice for every v ∉ S_0; K°_h = ∏_{v∉S_0} U_h(O_v), K° = ∏_{v∉S_0} G(O_v); 𝒮°(U_h(F_v)), 𝒮°(G(F_v)) the spherical Hecke algebras (units the characteristic functions), the local base-change homomorphisms BC_{h,v}: 𝒮°(G(F_v)) → 𝒮°(U_h(F_v)) and BC^{S_0}_h = ⊗_{v∉S_0} BC_{h,v}; 𝒮°(G(A)), 𝒮°(U_h(A)) the bi-K°- and bi-K°_h-invariant Schwartz functions.
items.note: The unramified base-change homomorphism of Hecke algebras (Satake) for U_h ⊂ Res_{E/F} GL.

items.name: Transfer of test functions between G and the U_h
items.statement: For h ∈ ℋ°, f_{S_0} ∈ 𝒮(G(F_{S_0})) and f^h_{S_0} ∈ 𝒮(U_h(F_{S_0})) are transfers if they have matching regular orbital integrals in the sense of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, Definition 4.4, with the Haar measures of §2.3.3.
items.note: Jacquet–Rallis smooth transfer as already planned in this candidate (local matching and transfer factors, ZHANG-21; global Definition 4.4, BPLZZ).

items.name: The Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma and transfer at split places
items.statement: The characteristic function 1_{G(O_v)} and the unit of the spherical Hecke algebra of U_h(F_v) are transfers at inert places v ∉ S_0 for h ∈ ℋ°, and 1_{G(O_v)} transfers to 0 on U_h(F_v) for h ∉ ℋ° at a suitable inert v (Yun 2011; Beuzart-Plessis, Duke 2021); at split places the transfer is explicit (W. Zhang, Ann. of Math. 2014, Prop. 2.5). Consequently the hypotheses of Proposition 10.1.6.1 are stable under enlarging S_0 (Remark 10.1.6.2).
items.locator: Remark 10.1.6.2 and proof of Proposition 10.1.6.1, pp. 320–321
items.note: The fundamental lemma for all residue characteristics is in this candidate through Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu; the paper leaves the bookkeeping of Haar measures to the reader.

items.name: Existence of smooth transfer (Zhang; Xue)
items.statement: At non-archimedean places every f^h_v ∈ 𝒮(U_h(F_v)) admits a transfer in 𝒮(G(F_v)), with the zero function on the other U_{h′}(F_v) (W. Zhang, Ann. of Math. 2014); at archimedean places the functions admitting transfers are dense (Xue, Crelle 2019), which suffices for continuous identities; combined, suitable families of test functions satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 10.1.6.1 exist with prescribed non-zero value of either side.
items.note: Proposition 4.6 of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, already in this candidate.

items.name: The unitary Jacquet–Rallis trace formula for Schwartz functions and the comparison of geometric sides
items.statement: For each h ∈ ℋ there is a distribution J^h on 𝒮(U_h(A)) (Zydor, Crelle 2020, Thm. 0.3 for C_c^∞; Chaudouard–Zydor, Compositio 2021, §1.1.3 and Thm. 15.2.3.1 for Schwartz functions) with the spectral description used below, and for f, (f^h) satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 10.1.6.1, I(f) = Σ_{h∈ℋ°} J^h(f^h) (Chaudouard–Zydor, Thm. 1.6.1.1) (10.1.6.4).
items.note: Chaudouard–Zydor's comparison of all geometric terms for matching functions (singular transfer), already listed in this candidate as BPLZZ Proposition 4.7.

items.name: Isolating the Hermitian Arthur parameter by multipliers compatible with transfer
items.statement: With the S′_0-multiplier algebras ℳ^{S′_0}(G(A)), ℳ^{S′_0}(U_h(A)) (Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, Def. 3.5): by Ramakrishnan's theorem and BPLZZ Theorem 3.19 there is μ ∈ ℳ^{S′_0}(G(A)) with μ(Π) = 1 and K^0_{μ∗f,χ′} = 0 for every χ′ ≠ χ with central character trivial on A_G; by BPLZZ Theorems 3.6 and 4.14(3)–(4) there are μ^h with μ^h(σ) = 1 for (U_h, σ) ∈ 𝔛^h_0 and K^{U_h}_{P,μ^h∗f^h,χ′} = 0 for χ′ ∉ 𝔛^h_0 and all P; and by BPLZZ Proposition 4.8 and Lemma 4.12 μ, μ^h can be chosen so that μ∗f, μ^h∗f^h still satisfy the hypotheses of Proposition 10.1.6.1. The common infinitesimal character: every (U_h, σ) ∈ 𝔛^h_0 has infinitesimal character with base change ξ_Π.
items.note: The paper cites these as BPLZZ Theorems 3.17, 4.12(3)–(4) and Lemma 4.10, the arXiv v1 numbering (sourceIssues E2). The infinitesimal-character statement is BPLZZ Theorem 4.14(4) for a non-cuspidal base change, whose printed proof has a gap (sourceIssues E1; PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21/E1); the design must take it from the repaired proof or from Mok and KMSW.

items.name: Proposition 10.1.6.1: the spectral identity of relative trace formulas
items.statement: Let Π = Ind^G_P(π) be a Hermitian Arthur parameter (χ regular and relevant) admitting K°-fixed vectors, S′_0 the union of S_0 ∖ V_{F,∞} and the finite places inert in E, and 𝔛^h_0 the classes (U_h, σ) with σ K°_h-unramified and split base change Π_v at all v ∉ S′_0 ∪ V_{F,∞}. Let f ∈ 𝒮°(G(A)) and f^h ∈ 𝒮°(U_h(A)) (h ∈ ℋ°) with (1) f = (Δ^{S_0,*}_HΔ^{S_0,*}_{G′})f_{S_0} ⊗ f^{S_0}, (2) f^h = (Δ^{S_0}_{U′_h})²f^h_{S_0} ⊗ f^{h,S_0}, (3) f_{S_0}, f^h_{S_0} transfers, (4) f^{h,S_0} = BC^{S_0}_h(f^{S_0}), (5) f^{S_0} a product of a smooth compactly supported function on ∏′_{v∉S′_0} G(F_v) and 1_{∏_{v∈S′_0∖S_0} G(O_v)}. Then Σ_{h∈ℋ°} J^h_{𝔛^h_0}(f^h) = 2^{−dim a_P}I_Π(f) = 2^{−dim a_P}I_{P,π}(f) (10.1.6.3).
items.note: Follows the proof of BPLZZ Theorem 1.8: (10.1.6.4) for μ∗f and μ^h∗f^h, then Theorem 3.3.9.1 and (10.1.5.2) I_χ = 2^{−dim a_P}I_{P,π} = 2^{−dim a_P}I_Π. The GRS descent gives some h with 𝔛^h_0 ≠ ∅ (printed '𝔛^h_π', sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Local relative characters I_{Π_v} and J_{σ_v} and the factorisation of I_Π
items.statement: For tempered Π_v: I_{Π_v}(f_v) = Σ_{W_v} λ_v(Π_v(f_v)W_v)\overline{β_{η,v}(W_v)}/⟨W_v, W_v⟩_{Whitt,v} over a K_v-basis of W(Π_v, ψ_{N,v}), with λ_v(W_v) = ∫_{N_H(F_v)∖H(F_v)} W_v, β_{η,v}(W_v) = ∫_{N′(F_v)∖𝒫′(F_v)} W_vη_{G′,v}, ⟨W_v, W_v⟩ = ∫_{N(F_v)∖𝒫(F_v)} |W_v|² (absolutely convergent, Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika Prop. 8.4); J_{σ_v}(f^h_v) = ∫_{U′_h(F_v)} Trace(σ_v(h_v)σ_v(f^h_v)) dh_v (Harris), with J_{σ_v}(1_{U_h(O_v)}) = Δ^{−2}_{U′_h,v}L(½, Π_v)/L(1, σ_v, Ad) for v ∉ S_0. For f = Δ^{S_0,*}_HΔ^{S_0,*}_{G′}∏_{v∈S_0}f_v × ∏_{v∉S_0}1_{G(O_v)}: I_Π(f) = L^{S_0}(½, Π)/L^{S_0}(1, Π, As^−_G) ∏_{v∈S_0} I_{Π_v}(f_v) (10.3.3.2), with L^{S_0}(s, Π, As^−_G) = L^{S_0}(s, Π_n, As^{(−1)^n})L^{S_0}(s, Π_{n+1}, As^{(−1)^{n+1}}) = L^{S_0}(s, σ, Ad).
items.note: Local spherical characters of Harris and Beuzart-Plessis.

items.name: Beuzart-Plessis's comparison of local relative characters
items.statement: If Π_v is the local base change of the tempered σ_v and f_v, f^h_v are transfers (v ∈ S_0), then I_{Π_v}(f_v) = κ_vJ_{σ_v}(f^h_v) with explicit κ_v ∈ ℂ^× and ∏_{v∈S_0} κ_v = 1 (Beuzart-Plessis, Invent. Math. 2021, Thm. 5.4.1).
items.note: Lemma 4.9 of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu uses the same comparison; already in this candidate.

items.name: The local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for tempered unitary pairs
items.statement: In a tempered Vogan L-packet of U(n) × U(n+1) over a local field, exactly one member supports a non-zero continuous U′_h(F_v)-invariant form (Beuzart-Plessis, Astérisque 418 (2020), and earlier p-adic work); with Mok and KMSW's description of cuspidal representations of U_h through local L-packets, only σ itself contributes to the left side of (10.3.4.3).
items.note: Local conjecture statement and cited theorems belong to this candidate; BPLZZ already added the tempered unitary case.

items.name: Mok and Kaletha–Mínguez–Shin–White: base change of tempered cuspidal representations of unitary groups
items.statement: A cuspidal σ on U_h(A) tempered everywhere has a weak base change Π to G, which is a strong base change (Π_v the local base change of σ_v at every v, local base change of ramified representations characterised by character relations); in particular Π is tempered everywhere and σ is described by local L-packets.
items.note: The endoscopic classification for unitary groups is ML.4.

items.name: Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent
items.statement: Every Hermitian Arthur parameter Π of G is the weak base change of a cuspidal σ on U_h(A) for some h ∈ ℋ° (any quasi-split hermitian form unramified outside S_0).
items.note: Automorphic descent (Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry 2011) is ML.5.

items.name: Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika: Rankin–Selberg integrals for GL_n × GL_{n+1}
items.statement: For cuspidal data the global zeta integral Z^RS(s, W) of a Whittaker function factors into local integrals, continues meromorphically with a functional equation, and represents L(s + ½, Π) (in the introduction's normalisation), the local integrals at unramified places giving the local L-factors; the local integrals converge absolutely for tempered Π_v (Prop. 8.4).
items.note: Rankin–Selberg theory for GL_n × GL_m, including Jacquet's archimedean integrals, is AL.3.

items.name: LF spaces, quasi-completeness and vector-valued integrals and sums
items.statement: A LCTVS is a Hausdorff locally convex space over ℂ; LF spaces are countable inductive limits of Fréchet spaces (strict when the connecting maps are closed embeddings); V_B for bounded absolutely convex B; quasi-complete spaces (Fréchet and strict LF spaces are).
