For X σ-compact locally compact with a Radon measure and V quasi-complete, an absolutely integrable continuous f: X → V (∫ p(f) < ∞ for every continuous seminorm p) has a unique ∫_X f ∈ V with ⟨λ, ∫f⟩ = ∫⟨λ, f⟩; summable and absolutely summable families (v_i)_{i∈I} and their sums.
items.note: Mathlib has locally convex spaces, seminorm families and barrelled spaces but no LF spaces, quasi-completeness or Pettis-type integrals in LCTVS.

items.name: Holomorphic functions valued in LCTVS and the Banach–Steinhaus consequences for LF spaces
items.statement: For V quasi-complete, a function on a complex manifold is holomorphic iff continuous and scalarly holomorphic on a total subspace of V′ (A.0.3.1; Bourbaki). LF spaces are barrelled (Trèves, Cor. 33.3), so bounded subsets of Hom(V, W) are equicontinuous and Hom(V, W) is quasi-complete for W quasi-complete; hence (A.0.4.2) s ↦ T_s(v_{s,k}) is continuous and holomorphic for holomorphic T and continuous-holomorphic v, (A.0.4.3) a holomorphic family T_s ∈ Hom(V, W) on U ⊂ M whose values T_s(v) all continue analytically to M continues as a holomorphic family of continuous maps, and the same for separately continuous bilinear forms (A.0.5.4)–(A.0.5.5).
items.note: Used for the holomorphy statements of §§6–7 (Corollary 2.9.7.2, Proposition 6.4.0.2, Theorem 7.1.3.1).

items.name: The Banach–Steinhaus theorem for barrelled spaces
items.statement: A pointwise bounded family of continuous linear maps from a barrelled space into a space with topology given by seminorms is (uniformly) equicontinuous.
items.locator: Appendix A, A.0.4, p. 328; used in Lemma 2.10.1.1, Theorem 3.3.7.1 and Lemma A.0.9.1
items.note: Mathlib's WithSeminorms.banach_steinhaus and PolynormableSpace.banach_steinhaus (Mathlib/Analysis/LocallyConvex/Barrelled.lean); Mathlib provides BarrelledSpace for Baire (e.g. Fréchet) spaces, not for LF spaces.

items.name: Nuclear maps turn summable families into absolutely summable ones
items.statement: Lemma A.0.6.1: if T: V → W is a nuclear map of LCTVS (Trèves, Defs. 47.2–47.3), then for every summable family (v_i) in V, (T(v_i)) is absolutely summable in W. Lemma A.0.6.2: a summable family (z_i) of complex numbers is absolutely summable with Σ|z_i| ≤ 4 sup_J |Σ_{i∈J} z_i|.
items.locator: Appendix A, A.0.6, Lemmas A.0.6.1–A.0.6.2, pp. 329–330
items.note: The mechanism behind the absolute summability in Theorem 2.9.4.1.

items.name: Completed projective tensor products and Grothendieck's description
items.statement: V ⊗̂ W with the universal property Hom(V ⊗̂ W, U) ≃ Bil(V, W; U) for complete U, and T ⊗̂ S. If V, W are spaces of functions on X, Y with topologies finer than pointwise convergence and V is a complete nuclear LF space, V ⊗ W → F(X × Y) extends to an embedding V ⊗̂ W ↪ F(X × Y) whose image is the set of f with f(x, ·) in the completion of W for every x and x ↦ ⟨f(x, ·), λ⟩ in V for every λ ∈ W′ (Grothendieck, Produits tensoriels, Ch. II, §3, n°3, Thm. 13) (A.0.7.8).
items.note: AS.0 plans nuclear Fréchet test-function spaces; completed tensor products are also required by AL.3.

items.name: Schwartz functions valued in a quasi-complete space and Lemma A.0.9.1
items.statement: For a real vector space 𝒜 and V quasi-complete, 𝒮(𝒜, V) consists of smooth f with Df bounded for all polynomial differential operators D; T ∘ f ∈ 𝒮(𝒜, W) for continuous T. Lemma A.0.9.1: if V is quasi-complete and barrelled and s ↦ Z_s ∈ V′ (s ∈ ℋ_{>C}) is holomorphic of order at most d in vertical strips on each v, then for f ∈ 𝒮(𝒜, V), s ↦ (λ ↦ Z_s(f_λ)) ∈ 𝒮(𝒜) is holomorphic of finite order in vertical strips. Orders in vertical strips are as in A.0.8.
items.locator: Appendix A, A.0.8–A.0.9, Lemma A.0.9.1, pp. 331–332
items.note: Mathlib's SchwartzMap covers normed targets only.

items.name: Vector-valued Phragmén–Lindelöf principles: Lemma A.0.10.1 and Corollaries A.0.11.1–A.0.11.2
items.statement: Lemma A.0.10.1: for V quasi-complete and holomorphic Z_+, Z_−: ℋ_{>C} → V of finite order in vertical strips such that λ ∘ Z_± extend to entire functions of finite order with λ ∘ Z_+(s) = λ ∘ Z_−(−s) for λ in a total subspace H ⊂ V′, Z_± extend to entire V-valued functions of finite order with Z_+(s) = Z_−(−s). Corollary A.0.11.1 (V = 𝒮(𝒜)): if Z_±(·, s) ∈ 𝒮(𝒜) holomorphically of finite order on ℋ_{>C} and each Z_±(λ, ·) is entire of finite order with Z_+(λ, s) = Z_−(λ, −s), then s ↦ Z_±(·, s) ∈ 𝒮(𝒜) is entire. Corollary A.0.11.2 (V = W′ for an LF space W): if Z_±(s, ·) ∈ W′ for s ∈ ℋ_{>C}, of order ≤ d on each w, and s ↦ Z_±(s, f) extends entirely with Z_+(s, f) = Z_−(−s, f) for f in a dense subset H ⊂ W, then Z_± extend to entire W′-valued functions with the functional equation for every w.
items.note: Proved by a Cauchy-integral representation after multiplying by e^{s^{4n+2}} and the classical Phragmén–Lindelöf principle; the key tool for Theorems 6.2.5.1(2) and 7.1.3.1.

items.name: The Phragmén–Lindelöf principle in a vertical strip
items.statement: A function differentiable on an open vertical strip, continuous on its closure, of growth at most exp(B exp(c|Im z|)) with c < π/(b − a), and bounded by C on the boundary lines is bounded by C on the closed strip.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.0.10.1, p. 332
items.note: Mathlib's PhragmenLindelof.vertical_strip (Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/PhragmenLindelof.lean) for functions valued in a normed space.

routes.brief: Part II of Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors). It starts where AL.3 stops. AL.3 plans Rankin–Selberg integrals and their period comparisons for cusp forms on GL_n × GL_m. AL.4 plans unramified Euler factors. This Part II adds the Asai L-function of GL_n(A_E) for a quadratic E/F. It also adds the two periods of the Jacquet–Rallis double quotient, evaluated on non-cuspidal (Eisenstein and moderate-growth) functions: the Flicker–Rallis period over GL_n(A_F) and the Rankin–Selberg period over the diagonal GL_n in GL_n × GL_{n+1}. Source: Beuzart-Plessis–Chaudouard–Zydor, 'The global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for unitary groups: the endoscopic case' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 135 (2022), 183–336), §§4, 6, 7, 9, §5.1.4, §8.1.2 and Lemmas 2.6.1.1, 2.6.2.1. Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 4.3.3.1: for f ∈ 𝒮(G_n(A)) and a ∗-regular datum χ = (M_P, π), ∫_{[G′_n]} K_χ(g, h) dh = 2^{−dim a_P}J_{P,π}(g, f), a discrete sum built from Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski intertwining periods. Theorem 6.2.5.1(2) and Theorem 6.2.6.1: for f ∈ 𝒮_χ([G_n]), χ ∗-regular with k blocks, lim_{s→1+}(s − 1)Z^FR_ψ(s, ⁰f, φ) = 2^{1−k}φ̂(0)β_n(W_{f,Π}) if χ is distinguished (0 otherwise) and φ̂(0)∫_{[G′_n]} f = ½ of it (Corollary 6.2.7.1). Theorem 7.1.3.1: for H-regular χ the diagonal period extends continuously from 𝒮_χ([G]) to 𝒯_χ([G]), and Z^RS_ψ(s, f) is entire with P_H(f) = Z^RS_ψ(0, f). Theorem 8.1.2.1: ⟨φ, φ⟩_Pet = ⟨W_φ, W_φ⟩_Whitt for Π induced from a regular datum. Theorem 9.2.5.1: J_η(φ) = β_η(W_φ) for relevant ∗-regular data, from the local Theorem 9.1.7.1, β_G(W(ϕ)) = ∫_{P_F∖G_F} β_M(ϕ(g)) dg. Cover, in this order: (1) Flicker–Rallis periods of cusp forms, distinction and the dichotomy for conjugate self-dual representations; the Asai L-function of an induced representation (Shahidi; Goldberg), its factorisation, continuation, functional equation, finite order in vertical strips (Finis–Lapid) and poles; (2) Flicker's global Asai integral and its unramified computation; Beuzart-Plessis's local Asai zeta integrals (continuation, functional equation, archimedean theory); the Flicker functional β_n and β_η; (3) the Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski intertwining periods J, J_Q, J_η, the (G, M)-family J_{Q,π} (Proposition 4.1.9.1) and its Schwartz property (Proposition 4.1.10.1); the mixed truncation Λ^T_m with Lemmas 4.2.3.1–4.2.3.2 and Proposition 4.2.3.3; ∗-regular data; Propositions 4.3.4.1, 4.3.6.1, 4.3.7.1, Lemmas 4.3.6.2 (JLR Theorem 40) and 4.3.7.2, and Theorem 4.3.3.1; (4) Lemmas 2.6.1.1–2.6.2.1, the Whittaker functions of moderate-growth functions, the zeta integral Z^FR_ψ, Theorem 6.2.5.1, the Epstein–Eisenstein series, Lemma 6.4.0.1, Proposition 6.4.0.2, Theorem 6.2.6.1 and Corollary 6.2.7.1; (5) the Ichino–Yamana truncation Λ^T_r (Proposition 3.3.2.1), the regularised Rankin–Selberg period of Eisenstein series (Proposition 5.1.4.1), Z^RS_ψ, H-regular data, Lemma 7.1.1.1, Proposition 7.2.0.2 and Theorem 7.1.3.1; λ, β_η, ⟨·,·⟩_Whitt and Theorem 8.1.2.1; Ichino–Yamana's identification λ(W_φ) = I(φ, 0) and its non-vanishing criterion; (6) the local Flicker functionals and Jacquet integrals of §9.1, Theorem 9.1.7.1 with Lemmas 9.1.7.3–9.1.7.7, and Theorem 9.2.5.1. State the archimedean case of Theorem 9.1.7.1 as a proof obligation, since the paper only sketches the variant of Baruch's theorem for P_F-invariant distributions on G/G_F. Use the corrected statements of sourceIssues E3, E8 and E9. Tests: n = 1, where Z^FR is Tate's integral for η-twisted Hecke characters and β_1 is a residue of a Hecke L-function; the split case E = F × F, where the Flicker–Rallis period becomes the Petersson inner product and Theorem 9.1.7.1 is Feigon–Lapid–Offen, Proposition A.2. Beuzart-Plessis–Chaudouard–Zydor (Publ. Math. IHÉS 135 (2022)) is one of the consumers that brief names. Take it from Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu Theorem 4.14(4) (the Annals numbering) with its Proposition 4.13(1) repaired: suppose 𝔇(G′, 1)^♥_{χ′} = ∅ and isolate with Theorem 3.19 instead of Theorem 3.6 (PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21/E1). sourceIssues.reason: The cited result is BPLZZ Theorem 4.14(4): if the weak base change of π exists and is hermitian, the base change of χ_{π_∞} is χ_{BC(π)_∞}.
